heroine.intro: The Shrine Maiden is the young keeper of the shrine at the top of the long stone steps, and the first person you meet after falling through the barrier from the outside world. She lives at the shrine itself: she sleeps in her own room off the east corridor of the main building, cooks at the kamado, drinks tea at the hall's tea table and on the veranda, and spends her days sweeping the approach, tending the grounds and praying at the altar. She is blunt, a little lazy and always short of money, and much kinder underneath than she will ever admit.
appearance: Everyday outfit: the shrine maiden set. A red bodice under a white collar with a soft cream knot at the chest, white detached sleeves that reach the wrist and flare at the cuff, a red shrine maiden skirt, and socks and loafers.
Colors: 'Shrine red' is her main cloth color and white the second. Fair skin and 'Oxblood' red eyes.
Hair: long, in a deep 'Shrine brown'. A fringe of blunt locks stops above her eyes, and side locks fall in front of her shoulders, each tied with a red and white wrapped tube.
Headwear: her signature huge bow, two wide red wings raised behind her head, frilled in white along the outer edge, with two short tails.
Face: a 'Deadpan' default expression. It changes with how she feels (happy, smiling, embarrassed, surprised, annoyed, angry, sad, sleepy, smug, worried).
Sleepwear: at night she wears a cream and white yukata with its obi, plus tabi and zori, and puts her everyday clothes back on in the morning.

Walk style: 'Relaxed'. Easygoing, weight on one leg, in no hurry. When she hurries over to welcome you back after a long time away, she uses a cheerful, slightly quicker step, then returns to her usual pace.
Rest pose: 'Laid back'. She stands loose and easy, weight on one leg.

Planned: her posture will follow her feelings (a cheerful walk when happy, arms crossed when annoyed, hands tucked into her sleeves outdoors in winter) and she will fidget when idle (yawning, tapping her foot, fixing her bow, fanning herself in summer). These reactions are designed but not in the game yet.
personality: Traits: blunt, carefree, lazy outside of duty but dutiful when it counts, kind underneath, very intuitive, flustered by affection, always hoping for donations, impartial (she is equally blunt with everyone), and slow to warm up.
How she speaks: casual and dry, in short, plain sentences. Typical sounds are 'Hmph.', 'Hm?', 'Hey!', '...!' when flustered and 'Fuaah...' when sleepy.
How she addresses you: 'you there' or 'visitor' as a stranger, plain 'you' as an acquaintance, your name once you are friends, and at the very end of the romance path sometimes 'dummy'.
Base mood: mildly cheerful, a little tired, a touch smug. Her feelings drift back to this calm baseline over time, and she forgives fairly easily.

Emotions she can feel: joy, affection, shyness, surprise, annoyance, anger, sadness, tiredness, smugness and worry. Each shows on her portrait and her face, and can show as an icon over her head (a note, a heart, a blush, '!', a sweat drop, an anger mark, a tear, 'z', a sparkle, '?').

She knows why she feels what she feels. If you upset her she can tell you so ('You know what you did. I'm not spelling it out.'), and if something else upset her, such as rain on her laundry, she tells you it is not your fault ('Someone else got on my nerves. Not your problem.').
Before you get close she is indifferent rather than shy. The flustered, stammering side only shows once real feelings are involved.

She talks on her own. When you are near and she is free, a speech balloon pops up about what she is doing, the weather, the hour, the season, the moon, how she feels, a memory, or you. She also comments on what you do near her: digging up the grounds, felling trees, fighting, getting hurt, ringing the bell, swimming, entering her room. Asleep, she mumbles. How often she does this is set in the settings under 'NPC chatter': Many, Normal, Few or None.

She reads the player: a female or male player, an outsider, or someone who changed into a fairy, youkai, ghost, god or other race is received differently. As the youkai-hunting shrine maiden she is warier of most non-human races, but a close bond outweighs that.
likes: Donations and offerings in the box
Quiet days with nothing going on

schedule.activity: Asleep on her futon in her room, in her yukata. She wakes somewhere between 05:30 and 06:40.
Sits up on the futon, folds it away, gets dressed for the day and says her morning prayer, almost every single day.
Stretches outside on many clear mornings and opens her room window to air it out.
Cooks breakfast at the kamado and eats it.

Makes tea and sits with it. From 07:00 she changes the offering at her household altar (if you have built one for her). From 08:00 she puts out last night's stone lanterns and, on some clear days, performs the purification rite and then puts the shrine tools away. She checks the offering box on about half of the days, tidies the altar, and from 09:00 writes ofuda and takes them to the altar. She also tidies her room and reads, more often when it rains.
Sweeps the approach and the courtyard on clear days, or the hall floor when it rains. Tends the grounds by the branch shrine, watches the sky, and has lunch between 11:30 and 13:15.

More tea and sweeping, reading on the veranda or by the lamp, feeding the koi from the bridge on clear days, writing ofuda, and a purification rite on some days. She naps only when she is tired. With the matching furniture she also studies scrolls at the alcove bookcase, sews on rainy afternoons, and warms herself or makes tea at the brazier.

Watches the sunset from the veranda on clear evenings, has tea there, feeds the koi, lights the stone lanterns and reads. From 18:30 she may close her room window, and dinner falls between 18:30 and 20:30.
Finishes dinner, then has an evening tea (after 20:00) at the tea table or her writing desk, reads, rests, sometimes writes a last ofuda, or sits by the brazier until about 21:30.
Says a short prayer at the altar before bed, closes her window, lays out the futon, changes into her yukata and goes to sleep. On average she is in bed around 22:00 and sleeps about eight hours.

schedule_notes: Time runs at one game minute per real second, so a full day lasts 24 real minutes. The day has six periods: late night (00:00-05:00), morning (05:00-11:00), midday (11:00-14:00), afternoon (14:00-17:30), sunset (17:30-19:30) and night (19:30-24:00).

Her day is not a fixed script. Within each period she picks from what fits the hour, the weather, the season, what she just did and how tired she is, so no two days are quite the same. Meals and prayers almost always happen on time.

Rain: she stays inside more (reading, resting, tea, writing ofuda, sweeping the hall instead of the courtyard) and skips the koi, the morning stretch, the purification rite and the lantern lighting. If rain finds her room window open, she drops what she is doing and goes to close it, unless she is asleep, getting up, getting dressed, praying or has food on the fire.

Seasons: in autumn and winter she spends time warming herself and making tea at the brazier in her room (if it is installed), and she also warms herself there on rainy days. In winter her writing desk becomes a kotatsu and a haori appears folded on the wardrobe.
Tired days: on about one day in five she wakes up tired. On those days she skips sweeping and takes an afternoon nap.

Visitors: ringing the bell at the offering box, or coming in from outside, counts as a visitor arriving. She comes over to greet you, but never while she is sleeping, getting up, getting dressed or praying, and not more than once every four hours.
There is no weekday schedule: every day follows the same pattern, shaped by weather, season and tiredness.
You can do things together with her between 07:00 and 22:30.
Planned: when an incident breaks out she will drop everything to investigate, and you will be able to go along. The behavior is designed, but incidents do not happen in the game yet.
meeting: She finds you first. The first time she lays eyes on you, she is startled to find someone from the outside world at her shrine's door. Her reaction depends on the hour ('Noon, and someone in weird clothes at my door. Wonderful.') and she remembers that first sight.
To talk, right-click her to open her window. Under Interactions, open Talk and choose Greet her.
Your whole first conversation counts as meeting a stranger. After it ends, she knows you, and from your next talk on you are acquaintances.

As an outsider, the first conversations and days are about where you came from: she explains the barrier, warns you that youkai eat outsiders, offers to send you home, and asks how you got here, whether you want to go back, and what life is like outside. This fades over the days and stops once you are no longer an outsider.

First steps: come back on different days (constancy builds Trust), and do quiet things with her from the Together menu, such as tea, sitting together, sweeping or tending the grounds. Once she knows you, praise her work while she is working.

Things to avoid at first: teasing a stranger lands badly with her, and so do prying questions too early, offering help before she trusts you, pestering her while she works, and waking her up. Later, speaking tenderly before you are best friends also backfires.
Your first real goal is the Friend milestone: Favor 20, Trust 15, three different days spent together, and two different kinds of activities.
relationship: Three bars show in her interaction panel, each from 0 to 100.
Favor is her general good will. It rises with help with chores, tea, compliments and gifts, and falls when you are a nuisance or keep insisting.

Trust is confidence built by constancy. It rises when you come back on different days, help without being asked, respect a refusal, talk with her properly and answer her questions well. It falls when you insist after a 'no', are rude, or wake her up.

Intimacy is the comfort of time spent together. It rises with quiet activities together (tea, sitting, reading, meals, the koi) and with gestures she accepts. It falls slowly if you stay away for a long time.

Raises her opinion: sweeping or tending the grounds together (+3 Favor, +3 or +2 Trust), tea together (+2 Favor, +3 Intimacy), sitting together (+3 Intimacy), reading or eating together (+3 Intimacy), cooking together, praying together (+3 Trust), walking together, feeding the koi together, good conversation (small talk, asking how she is, asking about her, sharing your day, teasing once you are close, praising her work, offering help), good answers to her questions, and the first time you install each piece of furniture you built for her room (+2 Favor, +1 Trust). Making her room cozy (Comfort 6) and a real home (Comfort 9) each give a one-time bonus.

Lowers her opinion: getting in her way (-1 Favor), waking her up (-1 Favor, -3 Trust), insisting after she said no (-1 Favor, -2 Trust), rude teasing (-1.5 Favor, -1 Trust), prying (-0.5 Favor, -0.5 Trust), being too forward (-0.5 Favor, -1 Trust), and answers that go against her (-1 Favor, -0.5 Trust). Insisting twice within seven days locks the matter for a week.

Repetition: most things only count once a day, and doing the same thing day after day gives less and less until you give it a few days' rest. Variety matters: different kinds of activities and different days are part of what the milestones ask for.
Absence: after seven days without seeing you, her Intimacy slowly drops (a quarter point per day). Milestones are never lost.
Strain: once you reach Love, letting Trust fall below 30 or Favor below 20 strains the relationship. Conversations go worse, and as a helper she will only do favors.

Who you are matters: with a female player, friendship grows faster but romance takes longer to click (she reads affection as friendship at first). With a male player she is more reserved at the start, insisting costs more, but romance moves faster once she trusts you. Fairies, youkai, gods, lunarians and some specific races get a warier welcome, and a close bond softens that.

Memory: she remembers what happens, with an importance scale running from trivial things forgotten within hours, to passing things (a day), notable things (two weeks), lasting things (two months) and things she never forgets (your first meeting, first conversation, firsts, milestones). Something that upset her becomes a grudge you can apologize for ('Apologize'). If something else upset her, you can 'Comfort her' instead.

Romance is your choice. It only starts if you open it with 'Show interest'. You can close it at any time with 'Stay friends': no penalty, friendship stays as it is, and you can reopen it after seven days. Friendship and romance are separate paths, and Best Friend never requires romance.

Planned: a mood of the day (good or bad days with reasons she can tell you), small needs (tea, food, rest, company, quiet, boredom), daily wishes, noticing your habits (daily visitor, sunset visitor, bell ringer...), inside jokes, and short scenes when you reach each milestone. These are designed but not active in the game yet.

milestones.name: Acquaintance
milestones.unlocks: Reached after your first full conversation. She calls you 'you' instead of 'visitor', teasing no longer offends her, 'Remember together' appears once you share memories, and you can ask her about her duty, youkai, incidents, money, sleep, flying, her god and going home. Her patience goes up to 3 topics per conversation.

milestones.name: Friend
milestones.unlocks: Needs Favor 20, Trust 15, 3 days together and 2 kinds of activities. She uses your name and lets you ask her to follow you ('Follow me'). The Compliment and Pat on the head gestures open up, plus Show interest (which starts the romance path) and Speak tenderly (though it still lands badly this early). She starts inviting you to tea (at the tea table or the brazier), meals, reading, feeding the koi and praying, and sometimes compliments you when you stand near. New talk topics are the barrier, festivals, banquets, what she wants and you. She will also do one favor a day for you as a helper. Patience: 4.

milestones.name: Best Friend
milestones.unlocks: Needs Friend, then Favor 40, Trust 50, Intimacy 45, 10 days together and 3 kinds of activities. Hug and Hold hands become available. She may hug you when you come back after a long time away, and may invite you to sit with her on the veranda at sunset. She opens up about her solitude and her past, and finally welcomes your offers of help. As a helper she now takes queued orders. Patience: 5. Does not require romance.

milestones.name: Yearning
milestones.unlocks: Romance path. Needs Friend, an open romance (Show interest accepted), Favor 35, Trust 30, Intimacy 35, and romantic moments on 2 different days and of 2 different kinds (for example sitting together at sunset, tea in the rain, a quiet walk, reading in the rain, dinner together at night, the koi at sunset). Hugs and holding hands open up even without Best Friend, along with the Forehead touch. She may take your hand on her own, and opens up about her fears and her future. Confess your feelings becomes possible once Favor 60, Trust 55 and Intimacy 60 are reached. It can only be done once; if she is not ready, wait three days.

milestones.name: Love
milestones.unlocks: Needs Yearning and an accepted confession, with Favor 60, Trust 55 and Intimacy 60. A new talk topic about 'us' opens, and her patience goes up to 6.

milestones.name: True Love
milestones.unlocks: Secret: it never appears in menus or status until you reach it. Needs Best Friend reached before Love, then Love, Favor, Trust and Intimacy at 85, romantic moments on 20 different days and of 4 kinds, 5 kinds of activities, 14 days since Love, no insisting after a refusal in the last 14 days, and a vow moment: sitting together at night under a clear sky. Her patience reaches 7, and she sometimes calls you 'dummy'.

together.name: Have tea together
together.text: Sit across the tea table in the hall and drink tea (20-60 minutes). One of the best ways to grow Intimacy. When it rains, it becomes a romantic 'tea in the rain' moment.

together.name: Tea by the brazier together
together.text: Tea for two at the brazier in her room. Needs the Brazier and the Guest Cushion installed. Counts the same as tea together.

together.name: Sit together
together.text: Sit side by side on the veranda (20-60 minutes). At sunset under a clear sky it becomes a romantic moment, and at night under a clear sky, once you are in love, it is where the vow moment happens.

together.name: Walk together
together.text: Stroll side by side on a clear day (15-40 minutes). A walk in the morning or at sunset is a 'quiet walk' moment.

together.name: Follow me
together.text: From Friend on, ask her to follow you (under Orders in her window). She walks behind you, even through doors, for 30 to 90 minutes, or until something urgent in her day calls her away (going to sleep, making and eating breakfast, her morning prayer). She waves goodbye when she leaves. It counts as walking together.

together.name: Walk hand in hand
together.text: On a clear day, holding hands turns your walk into a hand-in-hand stroll.

together.name: Sweep together
together.text: Sweep the approach or courtyard with her (20-50 minutes). Hard work that she appreciates: a big boost to Favor and Trust.

together.name: Tend the grounds together
together.text: Look after the grounds by the branch shrine together (15-40 minutes). Builds Favor and Trust.

together.name: Pray together
together.text: Pray side by side at the altar. Builds Trust.

together.name: Feed the koi together
together.text: Toss feed to the koi from the bridge over the pond, on clear days. At sunset it becomes a romantic moment.

together.name: Read together
together.text: Read side by side on the veranda. A rainy-day read together is a romantic moment.

together.name: Cook together
together.text: Share the work at the kamado: one cooks, the other tends the fire.

together.name: Eat together
together.text: Share a meal at the tea table. Dinner together at night is a romantic moment.

together.name: Her invitations
together.text: From Friend on, she sometimes comes to fetch you herself, beckons, and saves you a seat for a while when she is about to have tea, a meal, read, feed the koi, pray or sit by the brazier. From Best Friend (or Yearning) on, she may also invite you to watch the sunset. Just join her; if you don't come, she carries on alone. She takes at most three initiatives a day, with a break of an hour and a half in between.

together.name: Investigate together (planned)
together.text: Going with her to look into an incident, which gives a big Trust boost. Designed, but incidents do not happen in the game yet.

conversation: Greet her opens the conversation. Her greeting depends on your bond, the hour, her mood, how long it has been since you last talked and what she remembers, and sometimes she brings up a topic right away. Greeting counts as having talked today.

What you can say: Make small talk, How are you?, Ask about her, Tell her about your day, Tease her, Praise her work, Offer to help, Talk about donations, Remember together (from Acquaintance, once you share memories), Speak tenderly (from Friend), and Say goodbye. Apologize and Comfort her appear when they make sense.

Each line lands well, neutral or badly, depending on your bond, her mood, any strain between you, what she is doing, her memories and a bit of luck. Saying the same thing too often in one day gets an annoyed reply ('You said that already. I was listening, believe it or not.').

Her own tastes: teasing offends her as a stranger, is shrugged off as an acquaintance and is welcome from Friend on (better when she is happy, worse when she is annoyed or sad). Praise works best while she is doing chores. She refuses help until you are close (badly as a stranger, neutrally as an acquaintance or friend, gladly from Best Friend on), and offering while she rests or is annoyed goes worse. Speak tenderly backfires at Friend, is neutral at Best Friend and only lands well after that. Asking about her is too forward for a stranger. Telling her about your day goes worse when she is tired, annoyed or it is night. Money talk is usually neutral: it goes a little better on a day the box got an offering and worse when she is annoyed.

What you can ask about her opens up with the bond: the shrine, tea and outsiders from the start; her duty, youkai, incidents, money, sleep, flying, her god and going home as an acquaintance; the barrier, festivals, banquets, what she wants and you as a friend; her solitude and her past as a best friend; her fears and her future at Yearning; and 'us' at Love.

She asks back. After many of your lines there is a chance (higher the closer you are) that she asks you something, and then you can only pick an answer. An answer that suits her gives points and joy, a neutral one changes nothing, and one that goes against her costs points, annoys her and is remembered. The same question returns only after a few days, and she remembers what you said.

Some of her questions, with the answer she likes best: 'How do you take your tea?' (plain and hot, no fuss); 'When's the best time for a nap?' (right after lunch); 'Sweet or salty?' (sweet, obviously); 'Which chore would you skip forever?' (sweeping, the leaves never end); 'Rainy day plans?' (tea and absolutely nothing else); 'Say you found a pouch of coins?' (some goes in her offering box); 'If a youkai jumps you on the way down?' (run back here, fast); 'A certain witch keeps stealing my tea. What do I do?' (hide the good tea); 'Favorite season?' (winter, kotatsu season); 'Why do you think I keep doing this job?' (because someone has to); 'Do you believe in luck?' (sure, you'd buy one of her charms).

Questions for outsiders: what it's like outside now, whether you want to go back (she likes 'I like it here'), how you ended up at her door, what people eat out there, and what work you did. Closer bonds bring questions about whether you would come looking if she vanished, staying at the shrine, what she is to you and where you see yourself in ten years.

Patience: each line costs patience. She has 2 as a stranger, 3 as an acquaintance, 4 as a friend, 5 as a best friend or at Yearning, 6 at Love and 7 at True Love; one less when she is tired or annoyed, one more when she is happy. She recovers one point every 40 game minutes. When it runs out she ends the talk in her own way ('That's enough talking. I have a shrine to run. Bye.').
She cannot talk while she is asleep, getting changed or praying; her panel says so ('She is praying.').
gestures: Gestures you can offer (Gestures tab): Compliment and Pat on the head from Friend; Hold hands and Hug from Best Friend or Yearning; Show interest from Friend (this opens the romance path); Forehead touch from Yearning; Confess your feelings once, at Yearning with Favor 60, Trust 55 and Intimacy 60.

Gestures play out on the same playback bar as interactions (Getting close, Beginning, The moment, Ending), with adjustable speed and an End button (or Esc). Holding hands keeps going until you press End, walk off or jump.

She can say no. Trying something she is not ready for (a stranger going for a hug) gets a real reaction: she steps back or gives a soft 'no', with a line ('Hey! Since when do strangers hug shrine maidens?'), a change of mood and a memory. When she is tired she is more likely to refuse. Respecting a refusal earns Trust; insisting costs Favor and Trust.
The moment matters: romantic gestures go over better at sunset or at night, in the rain, or while sitting together, and the higher her Intimacy the better.

Gestures she starts on her own: a small wave the first time you come near her after you start playing, and another when you part after walking together. From Friend on she sometimes walks up and compliments you if you stand near her. From Best Friend or Yearning she may hug you when you come back after a long time away. At Yearning, with romance open, she may take your hand (and during a walk together her hand may find yours, turning it into a hand-in-hand walk) or lean in for a forehead touch. She never does Show interest or Confess for you; those are always your choices.
Everything she starts happens without a prompt. If you walk away or are busy, she simply goes back to what she was doing, with no penalty.
helper: She can help you with work. Right-click her and open 'Orders', or use the 'Board of orders', which shows her portrait, her order queue and her work ranks.

Friend: one favor per day. Chop a tree, Mine a block, or Put away what you carry. You pick the tree or block in the world and she walks there, does the job with her own axe or pickaxe, gathers the drops and brings them to you or puts them in a fitting chest.

Helper (after Friend; Trust 30, Favor 25, 5 days together): simple orders whenever you like, up to a daily cap of work hours. This adds 'Gather what lies there' and 'Bring more of this' (hold an item and she fetches up to a stack of it from a house chest).
Best Friend: queue up to 12 orders with Shift + click.

Work partner (after Best Friend; Trust 60, Favor 45, 5 days of finished work, 3 kinds of orders): 'Keep a chest stocked'. She keeps about 20 of what a chest holds (wood by default) during her shift from 08:00 to 18:00, first by moving items from another chest, then by chopping trees.
Daily work cap: half an hour as a friend, 3 hours as a helper, 5 as a best friend, 7 as a work partner. After that: 'That's enough work for today.'

When she won't (or not yet): in the rain ('In this rain? Once it stops.'), alone in the dark ('Alone in the dark? Only if you come with me.'), during her own routine (sleeping, getting up, getting dressed, praying, cooking and meals), when tired ('After some tea, all right?'), on festival days, and anything that belongs to the shrine ('I won't touch that. It belongs to the shrine.'). When the relationship is strained she only does favors. Waiting orders stay in her queue and she finishes them by herself when she can.

If she can't reach a target she marks it with a red X, says so once, and moves on; change the terrain near it and she goes back by herself. She starts with a basic axe and pickaxe, carries an 8-slot work bag, and likes putting things away best.
Planned: lending and equipping tools, her full inventory, work areas, more standing orders, a Steward rank that delegates to others, working while you travel, and a daily work summary.
room: Her room opens off the shoji door in the east corridor of the main building. Press E to go in and out. It is a young shrine maiden's room, warm and lived-in, with a light mess on the furniture (never in the way) and the season on show. By day cool light comes in through the window; at night the amber room lamp, the paper lantern and, if installed, the brazier's embers light it.

From the door to the right: the gohei stand, the room lamp with her household altar (once installed) on a shelf under the beam above it, the keepsake shelf, the futon, the dressing screen, the wardrobe (tansu), the writing desk under the window, the brazier corner (once installed) with a seat on each side and a guest cushion, the tokonoma alcove with a hanging scroll and the season's ikebana, and the alcove bookcase.

Belongings and decor: a hanging scroll, ikebana, drying flowers, a paper lantern, a tanzaku on a bamboo branch, an omamori on the wall, a bonsai on the sill and a wind chime, piles of books and a reading cushion, a small rug, a camellia in a pot, folded clothes (whichever outfit she is not wearing), teacups, a stack of ofuda, a writing set, and on the keepsake shelf a vase, a comb box, books and a spare ribbon.

The room tells you things: scattered cups and papers mean it needs tidying, the ofuda stack means a finished ofuda is ready to take, a swaying chime and flowers mean the window is open, and wilted sakaki on the altar means the offering needs changing.

Seasons: the ikebana changes every season, the tanzaku is fresh in summer and faded the rest of the year, and in winter the desk becomes a kotatsu (with a tangerine on top), the brazier glows and a haori sits folded on the wardrobe.

Furniture you can craft at the carpenter's bench and install through each spot's window (most pieces replace a plain version the house already has; the altar, brazier, guest cushion and sewing box are new additions): Futon Set (she wakes better rested), Folding Screen (painted with the season: flowers, waves, maple, snowy pine; it brightens her mornings), Tansu Cabinet (a real 36-slot chest; putting her tools away pleases her), Writing Desk (in keyaki; adds 'Take a finished ofuda'), Round Window (with a bamboo blind in summer; airing the room in spring and summer pleases her), Keepsake Shelf (looking at her keepsakes warms her heart), Room Lamp (brighter at night; reading at night is cozy), Scroll Shelves (she studies the scrolls in the afternoon and at sunset), Gohei Rack (putting her tools away pleases her), Sewing Box (she sews on rainy afternoons), Household Altar (she changes the offering every day), Brazier (she warms herself and makes green tea in autumn and winter, and it opens tea for two) and Guest Cushion (your seat at the brazier; needs the Brazier).

Comfort: each crafted piece adds Comfort by its quality (common 1, fine 2, masterwork 3), up to 10. At Comfort 3 (Good bed) she wakes up better rested. At Comfort 6 (Cozy) she rests even more and you get a one-time relationship bonus. At Comfort 9 (Home) you get a bigger one-time bonus. The first time you install each piece, she takes it as a gift.
trivia: She takes her tea plain and hot, no fuss, and admits she is on the third brew from the same leaves ('Still tea. Mostly.').
The empty offering box is the running joke of her life: she checks it, checks it again, and suspects it is broken because coins must vanish inside.
A certain witch keeps drinking her tea and never brings any. Her advice to you: hide the good tea.
Ringing the shrine bell on a day with no offering earns you a dry remark ('Ring all you like. The gods prefer coins.').
She calls sleep her favorite activity, and the best time for a nap is right after lunch. Waking her is one of the quickest ways to lose her Trust.
Her favorite season is winter, kotatsu season, but she thinks the shrine looks best in spring when the blossoms fall.
On rainy days she grumbles about laundry stuck indoors, and the roof leaks; if the shrine ever got rich, the first thing she would do is fix the roof.
Dig up the shrine grounds and she will shout at you ('Digging holes at a shrine? Who raised you?').
She talks to the koi while feeding them ('You lot eat better than I do.') and secretly finds the rings on the water calming.
She would rather do everything herself: offer a hand with her chores while you are still a stranger and you hear 'Hands off the broom. It's mine.'

creatures.name: Honeybee
creatures.habitat: Meadows of the Garden of the Sun; by day in spring and summer.
creatures.description: An amber bee with dark bands that flies between the flowers and its hive, a hollow log. It is harmless unless you stir it up. Then the whole swarm chases you for a while before it goes home.

creatures.name: Rhinoceros Beetle
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest and Forest of Magic; on summer nights. At the shrine: on the trees along the forest path.
creatures.description: A polished chestnut beetle with a long horn. It crawls slowly, climbs tree trunks and shoves any rival beetle it meets. If you startle one on a trunk, it lets go and drops.

creatures.name: Boar
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest and the open plains, in forests and fields; by day, all year. Never on the shrine grounds.
creatures.description: A heavy dark-brown boar with a pale tusk. It paws the ground and then charges in a straight line, so be ready to get out of the way.

creatures.name: Butterfly
creatures.habitat: Meadows of the Garden of the Sun, Nameless Hill and the plains; by day in spring and summer. At the shrine: along the shrine approach on fine days.
creatures.description: A yellow swallowtail with dark veins and a red spot on its hind wings. It zigzags from flower to flower and opens and closes its wings while it rests.

creatures.name: Chochin-obake
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the Forest of the Tanuki; at night, all year.
creatures.description: An old paper lantern that has come alive, with one big eye and a long red tongue. It floats along the road at night, lit from within, and laughs with its mouth wide open. When someone comes near it goes dark and drifts away. It fights only if provoked.

creatures.name: Cicada
creatures.habitat: Forests of the plains and the Great Youkai Forest; by day in summer. At the shrine: singing on the trees along the forest path.
creatures.description: A green-and-black cicada that clings to a tree trunk and sings. It goes quiet when you come close and flies off to another tree.

creatures.name: Bell Cricket
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the red lily fields; on autumn nights. At the shrine: in the grass at the foot of the stairway.
creatures.description: A small black cricket with pale wings. At night it raises its wings and sings in the grass, and the song stops as soon as you get close.

creatures.name: Mountain Crow
creatures.habitat: Youkai Mountain, the plains, the Hill of the Shrine, the Great Youkai Forest and the wasteland; by day and at dusk, all year, in snow as well. At the shrine: over the stairway, at its foot and in the courtyard.
creatures.description: A black bird with a blue sheen, said to carry messages for the tengu. It lands with its wings spread, walks and pecks at the ground, and caws. If provoked, it climbs above its target and dives at it.

creatures.name: Crow Tengu
creatures.habitat: Peaks of Youkai Mountain and fields of the plains; by day, all year. Rare.
creatures.description: A small tengu with black wings, a red tokin cap and a leaf fan. She follows you from a distance, branch to branch, and vanishes when you look her way. She fights back only if attacked.

creatures.name: Deer
creatures.habitat: Meadows and forests of the plains and Youkai Mountain; by day and at dusk, all year.
creatures.description: A sika deer with a spotted brown coat and a white tail. Deer graze in herds, and when one is startled the whole herd bounds away together. It never fights back.

creatures.name: Red Dragonfly
creatures.habitat: The Misty Lake and fields of the plains; by day in summer and autumn. At the shrine: over the pond.
creatures.description: A slender red dragonfly that hovers, darts and hovers again. It rests on the tips of things, such as the edge of a step.

creatures.name: Fairy
creatures.habitat: Almost everywhere in Gensokyo: fields, meadows, forests, lakes and rivers; by day, all year. At the shrine: the courtyard, the stairway, the pond and the forest path.
creatures.description: The common fairy of Gensokyo: small, in a blue dress and white apron, with glassy wings. She is mischievous but never really dangerous. She plays, naps and flees when hurt.

creatures.name: Autumn Leaf Fairy
creatures.habitat: Forests, Youkai Mountain and the Hill of the Shrine; by day in autumn. At the shrine: the forest path and the stairway.
creatures.description: A fairy with red-orange hair, a golden maple leaf pinned in it, a wine-red dress and wings like gold leaves. She comes out only in autumn.

creatures.name: Flower Fairy
creatures.habitat: Garden of the Sun and Nameless Hill; by day in spring and summer.
creatures.description: A tiny fairy who wears an upside-down bellflower as a cap, with a petal skirt and leaf wings. Buds open wherever she lands. She never fights back and simply flees if struck.

creatures.name: Ice Fairy
creatures.habitat: The Misty Lake, the plains, Youkai Mountain and the Hill of the Shrine; by day in winter, in snow as well. At the shrine: over the frozen pond and in the courtyard.
creatures.description: A frost-haired fairy with a snowflake clip and wings made of ice shards. She comes out in winter, and her attacks are cold.

creatures.name: Lake Fairy
creatures.habitat: Lake and shore of the Misty Lake; by day from spring to autumn.
creatures.description: A fairy with long sky-blue hair, a blue bow, a teal dress and glass wings. She skims over the lake by day.

creatures.name: Maid Fairy
creatures.habitat: The Misty Lake, home of the Mansion of the Lake; by day, all year. At the shrine: a rare visitor in the courtyard.
creatures.description: A fairy in a black dress, frilled apron and white headdress who serves at the mansion by the lake. Now and then one is sent to the shrine on an errand.

creatures.name: Fairy of the Dark
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest and Forest of Magic; at night, all year. At the shrine: the forest path after dark.
creatures.description: A fairy with short black hair, a crimson bow, a black dress and wings tinted violet. She comes out only at night.

creatures.name: Spring Fairy
creatures.habitat: The Hill of the Shrine, the plains, Nameless Hill and the forests; by day in spring. At the shrine: under the cherry trees of the shrine approach and in the courtyard.
creatures.description: A pink-haired fairy with a crown of little flowers, a green dress and round wings like cherry petals. She appears only in spring.

creatures.name: Sunflower Fairy
creatures.habitat: The Garden of the Sun, the plains, the Hill of the Shrine and the Misty Lake; by day in summer. At the shrine: the courtyard, the pond and the forest path.
creatures.description: A fairy with long brown hair, a sunflower behind her head and a dress the gold of summer fields. She appears only in summer.

creatures.name: Firefly
creatures.habitat: Rivers and shores of the Misty Lake and the Great Youkai Forest; on summer nights. At the shrine: over the pond.
creatures.description: A small black firefly whose lantern lights up the dark. Clouds of them glow and fade in waves over the water and drift slowly toward any nearby light.

creatures.name: Fox
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest and Forest of the Tanuki; at dusk and at night, all year. At the shrine: now and then on the forest path at dusk.
creatures.description: A slender red fox with a white-tipped tail and dark legs. It follows you from a distance and slips away when you turn to look. It bites back if attacked.

creatures.name: Mountain Frog
creatures.habitat: Near water on Youkai Mountain, the Misty Lake, the plains and the Hill of the Shrine; by day, at dusk and at night from spring to autumn, in rain as well. At the shrine: by the pond.
creatures.description: A small green frog that sits with its throat pulsing and hops about. It croaks with its throat puffed up like a bubble. It never fights back and flees when struck.

creatures.name: Funayuurei
creatures.habitat: Lakes and rivers of the Shore of the Sanzu and the Misty Lake; on summer nights, in rain as well. Never on the shrine grounds. Rare.
creatures.description: A ghost of those lost at sea, green-grey like deep water, that rises from the water holding out a ladle. It is hostile to anyone who comes near.

creatures.name: Living Geta
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the Hill of the Shrine; by day, all year. At the shrine: now and then on the shrine approach.
creatures.description: A single wooden clog that has come alive, with one big eye and its red thong as a tuft. It hops about looking for its lost partner, follows passers-by a little way and clacks when it lands. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Ghost
creatures.habitat: The Shore of the Sanzu, the Great Youkai Forest, the wasteland and the red lily fields; at night, all year, in any weather. Near the shrine, outside its safe grounds: now and then on the forest path after dark.
creatures.description: A round white ghost with a face and a tail like a flame. It floats straight through solid blocks. Before it strikes it turns cold and dark, its eyes burning, then rushes right through you.

creatures.name: Giant Salamander
creatures.habitat: Rivers of Youkai Mountain; at night, all year, in rain as well. Rare.
creatures.description: A huge, flat salamander with mottled brown skin that lies still on the river bed and slowly opens its wide mouth. It crawls along the bottom, snaps at passing fish and swims off when startled. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Hare
creatures.habitat: Fields and meadows of the plains and Nameless Hill; by day, all year.
creatures.description: A small hare with tall ears and a white tail. It sits still in the grass and bolts away in zigzags when startled.

creatures.name: Heron
creatures.habitat: Shore of the Misty Lake; by day from spring to autumn. At the shrine: now and then standing in the shallows of the pond.
creatures.description: A white heron with a long neck and a yellow beak. It stands motionless in the shallows, then suddenly strikes at a fish.

creatures.name: Hitodama
creatures.habitat: The Shore of the Sanzu and the red lily fields; at night, all year, in rain as well.
creatures.description: A faceless ball of cold blue-white fire with a trailing tail: the flame of a soul. Hitodama drift slowly in pairs toward the river. They are harmless.

creatures.name: Ittan-momen
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the wasteland; at night, all year. Never on the shrine grounds. Rare.
creatures.description: A long strip of old cotton cloth with glowing red eyes that ripples through the night sky. It rears its head, then drops down to wrap itself around anyone passing underneath.

creatures.name: Kamaitachi
creatures.habitat: Hills of Youkai Mountain and fields of the plains; by day and at night in autumn and winter. Never on the shrine grounds.
creatures.description: A long, low weasel with a chestnut coat and a sickle-shaped blade on each forepaw, which arrives with streaks of wind. It attacks anyone who crosses its path.

creatures.name: Kappa
creatures.habitat: Rivers, lakes and shores of Youkai Mountain, the Misty Lake and the Great Youkai Forest; by day and at dusk from spring to autumn. At the shrine: now and then by the pond.
creatures.description: A small river-folk girl with short blue hair, a green cap and a big pack, who stops to snack on a cucumber. The kappa are a people: she never fights back and runs off if struck.

creatures.name: Kappa Tinker
creatures.habitat: Rivers and shores of Youkai Mountain and the Misty Lake; by day from spring to autumn.
creatures.description: A kappa in a leather work apron with a red toolbox and a hammer. She mends things on the riverbank with sparks flying. She never fights back and dashes off when someone approaches.

creatures.name: Karakasa
creatures.habitat: Fields, forests and meadows of the plains, the Great Youkai Forest, the Forest of the Tanuki and the Hill of the Shrine; at dusk and at night, all year, in rain as well. At the shrine: on the stairway and at its foot.
creatures.description: An old lilac paper umbrella that has turned youkai, with one big eye, a long red tongue and a single leg in a wooden sandal. It hops about and spins open when it plays. If provoked, it shakes with laughter and lunges to lick you.

creatures.name: Katashiro
creatures.habitat: Fields of the Hill of the Shrine and the plains; by day, all year. At the shrine: now and then in the courtyard.
creatures.description: A paper offering doll that has come alive, with dot eyes and a red seal on its chest. It floats on the wind and copies you: it drifts as you walk, stops when you stop and flips over when you jump. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Kedama
creatures.habitat: Fields, meadows, forests and hills across Gensokyo, including the Hill of the Shrine; by day, at dusk and at night, all year. At the shrine: the stairway, its foot and the forest path.
creatures.description: A ball of white fur with two eyes that bounces about in flocks, rolls over when it plays and bursts into fluff when beaten. If provoked, its fur stands on end before it lunges.

creatures.name: Pink Kedama
creatures.habitat: Meadows of Nameless Hill and the plains; by day in spring.
creatures.description: A kedama with fur as pink as the lily-of-the-valley meadows in spring. A flock moves together, rolls down slopes and bounces off whatever it meets. It fights only if provoked.

creatures.name: Shadow Kedama
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest; at night, all year. Near the shrine, outside its safe grounds: the forest path at night.
creatures.description: A dark-furred kedama with gold eyes that shine in the dark. It hides in the shadows under the trees and springs at anyone who passes.

creatures.name: Snow Kedama
creatures.habitat: Peaks of Youkai Mountain; by day in winter, in snow as well.
creatures.description: A frost-white kedama that disappears into the snow while it keeps still. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Kingfisher
creatures.habitat: Rivers of the Misty Lake and the Great Youkai Forest; by day in spring and summer. At the shrine: now and then over the pond.
creatures.description: A small bird with a river-blue back, an orange breast and a long beak that keeps close to the water. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Foxfire
creatures.habitat: Forests of the Forest of the Tanuki and the Great Youkai Forest; on autumn and winter nights. At the shrine: the forest path at night.
creatures.description: An orange-gold flame that casts its own light in the dark. Rows of them glimmer far off under the trees. They are harmless.

creatures.name: Koi
creatures.habitat: Any pond or body of water large enough, including the shrine pond; all year, swimming slowly under the ice in winter.
creatures.description: Kohaku, Ogon and Showa koi that wander their pond and dart toward food pellets. When someone stops to feed them nearby, they gather beneath and wait.

creatures.name: Lily Wisp
creatures.habitat: The red lily fields along the Road of Reconsideration; at dusk and at night in autumn.
creatures.description: A red-pink flame that rises from the red lilies and glows softly in the dark. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Great Moth
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest and Forest of Magic; on summer and autumn nights. At the shrine: around the stone lanterns of the shrine approach and on the forest path.
creatures.description: A pale green moon moth with long tails and eyespots on its wings. It is drawn to any nearby light and circles it. If stirred up, it beats its wings at you in a cloud of scales.

creatures.name: Mountain Viper
creatures.habitat: Forests and hills of Youkai Mountain and the Great Youkai Forest; by day in summer and autumn. Near the shrine, outside its safe grounds: coiled in the brush by the forest path.
creatures.description: A grey-brown viper blotched like dead leaves that lies coiled and still in the brush. Step too close and it draws back into an S, then strikes.

creatures.name: Mountain Wolf
creatures.habitat: Peaks, hills and woods of Youkai Mountain; at night, all year, in snow as well. Never on the shrine grounds.
creatures.description: A long-legged grey wolf with a pale chest and a full, hanging tail that prowls the mountain at night. It attacks on sight.

creatures.name: Glowing Mushroom
creatures.habitat: Forest of Magic; at night, all year, in rain as well.
creatures.description: A sea-green mushroom with a bell-shaped cap that glows softly in the dark. When someone comes near, it shrinks down where it stands. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Walking Mushroom
creatures.habitat: Forest of Magic; by day and at night, all year, in rain as well.
creatures.description: A red mushroom with cream spots that waddles about on two stubby feet in a line with its fellows. If provoked, it swells up and puffs out a cloud of golden spores.

creatures.name: Nekomata
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the Forest of the Tanuki; at night, all year. Rare.
creatures.description: A slender black youkai cat with a white breast, two tails and gold eyes that shine in the dark. It fights back if attacked.

creatures.name: Night Heron
creatures.habitat: Shores of the Misty Lake and the Shore of the Sanzu; at night in summer and autumn. At the shrine: rarely, by the pond after dark.
creatures.description: A slate-grey heron with a white breast, a black crown and a red eye. It glows a faint blue in the dark, like the heron's fire of old tales.

creatures.name: Little Nurikabe
creatures.habitat: Fields and forests of the plains and the Great Youkai Forest; at night, all year, in rain as well. At the shrine: now and then on the forest path. Rare.
creatures.description: A small plaster wall under a cap of roof tiles that lies in wait on the road, looking like an ordinary wall. Once found out, it sprouts eyes and feet and sidesteps to block your way. If provoked, it leans back and shoves.

creatures.name: Onryo
creatures.habitat: The red lily fields and the wasteland; at night, all year, in rain as well. Never on the shrine grounds. Rare.
creatures.description: A vengeful white spirit veiled in long black hair, with one red eye glaring through. It hunts anyone it sees and passes straight through walls.

creatures.name: Otter
creatures.habitat: Rivers and shores of the Misty Lake and the Great Youkai Forest; at dusk, all year. At the shrine: now and then by the pond at dusk.
creatures.description: A long, low otter youkai with a dark brown coat and small round ears. It mischievously mimics your steps and fights back if attacked.

creatures.name: Owl
creatures.habitat: Great Youkai Forest and Forest of Magic; at night, all year. At the shrine: one on the forest path.
creatures.description: A brown owl with ear tufts and big gold eyes that shine in the dark. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Phantom Wisp
creatures.habitat: Peaks of Youkai Mountain and the Shore of the Sanzu; at any hour in winter, in snow as well.
creatures.description: A small, faceless wisp as white as rime, with a tail that frays into three strands and frost twinkling around it. It glows faintly in the dark and follows you closely.

creatures.name: Pheasant
creatures.habitat: Fields and meadows of the plains and the Forest of the Tanuki; by day, all year.
creatures.description: A bird with a dry-grass brown back, a green breast and a long pointed tail that walks hidden in the grass. Step close and it bursts into flight with a cry.

creatures.name: Youkai Rabbit
creatures.habitat: Bamboo Forest of the Lost, the forests and the plains; by day and at dusk, all year. At the shrine: now and then on the forest path and at the foot of the stairway.
creatures.description: A rabbit girl from the Bamboo Forest with tall cream ears, a pink dress and a wooden mochi mallet. She hops about, pounds mochi in a little mortar when she plays, and swings her mallet if provoked.

creatures.name: Lunar Rabbit
creatures.habitat: Bamboo Forest of the Lost; at night, all year. Rare.
creatures.description: A moon rabbit sentinel with long lavender hair, white ears and a dark blue coat. She strikes anyone who comes near, then goes back to her post.

creatures.name: White Rabbit
creatures.habitat: Bamboo Forest of the Lost; by day and at dusk, all year.
creatures.description: A silver-haired rabbit girl with white ears, a red dress and a mochi mallet. White rabbits roam in small bands and scatter in zigzags when startled.

creatures.name: Rat Snake
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the Forest of the Tanuki; by day from spring to autumn.
creatures.description: A long olive-green snake that climbs up walls and onto roofs as it goes. It is harmless.

creatures.name: River Carp
creatures.habitat: Rivers and lakes of the Misty Lake and the Great Youkai Forest; by day from spring to autumn, in rain as well.
creatures.description: A wild carp with an olive back, brassy scaled flanks and whiskers at its mouth. It swims against the current and now and then leaps out of the water. It is harmless.

creatures.name: River Crab
creatures.habitat: Shores and rivers of the Misty Lake and Youkai Mountain; by day and at night in summer, in rain as well. At the shrine: on the bank of the pond past the bridge.
creatures.description: A red-orange crab with stalked eyes that scuttles sideways along the bank and blows bubbles. Instead of running away, it backs off sideways with its claws raised and pinches anyone who gets too close.

creatures.name: Rokurokubi
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the Forest of the Tanuki; at night, all year. Rare.
creatures.description: A young woman in a pale wisteria kimono whose neck can stretch. She crosses the road at night with small steps and now and then stretches her neck up to peek around. She never fights back and runs off if struck.

creatures.name: Sake Jar
creatures.habitat: Fields of the Forest of the Tanuki and the plains; at dusk in autumn.
creatures.description: An old cream-clay sake flask with a flushed, happy face that waddles after passers-by. It pours a little cup as an offering and hiccups, and it rolls away when frightened. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Sanzu Crow
creatures.habitat: The Shore of the Sanzu and the red lily fields; at any hour, all year, in any weather.
creatures.description: A black crow with a red eye that perches on the stones along the river of the dead and follows the souls that cross.

creatures.name: Sanzu Fish
creatures.habitat: The river at the Shore of the Sanzu; at any hour, all year.
creatures.description: A fish made only of bones (skull, spine and ribs), pale as rime and faintly glowing. It swims the river of the dead and drifts up and down in slow curves. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Waiting Soul
creatures.habitat: Shore of the Sanzu; at any hour, all year, in rain as well.
creatures.description: A calm, pale violet soul waiting for the ferry, glowing faintly at night. Souls float in a row along the shore. They are harmless.

creatures.name: Serow
creatures.habitat: Peaks of Youkai Mountain; by day, all year. Rare.
creatures.description: A stocky dark-grey goat-antelope with a pale throat and two short black horns. It stands on the cliffs watching you and is gone the moment you look back.

creatures.name: Snow Monkey
creatures.habitat: Peaks and hills of Youkai Mountain; by day in autumn and winter, in snow as well.
creatures.description: A macaque with a grey-brown coat and a bare red face. Snow monkeys roam in troops and take fright together. Strike one and it calls the rest of the troop.

creatures.name: Sparrow
creatures.habitat: Fields and meadows of the plains and the Hill of the Shrine; by day, all year. At the shrine: a flock in the courtyard.
creatures.description: A small brown bird with a cream breast. Sparrows peck at the ground in flocks, and the whole flock takes off together when someone comes near.

creatures.name: Spore Puff
creatures.habitat: Forest of Magic; by day in summer and autumn, in rain as well. Never on the shrine grounds.
creatures.description: A plain brown mushroom that lies in wait, then sprouts eyes and feet. It swells its cap into a ball and bursts into a cloud of violet poison.

creatures.name: Lily-of-the-Valley Doll
creatures.habitat: Meadows of Nameless Hill; by day in spring. Never on the shrine grounds.
creatures.description: A doll dressed as a lily of the valley that lies in the meadow like a dropped toy. When someone comes near it wakes, walks stiffly and lets out a violet cloud of poison.

creatures.name: Swallow
creatures.habitat: Fields of the plains and the Garden of the Sun; by day in spring and summer.
creatures.description: A deep-blue swallow with a white breast and long tail streamers. It flies low and fast in curves over the fields and never lands on the ground.

creatures.name: Tanuki
creatures.habitat: Forest of the Tanuki; at night, all year.
creatures.description: A round grey-brown raccoon dog with a dark mask and a ringed tail. It pretends to be an ordinary object, like a pot or a stone, and jumps up when you come close. Strike it and it plays dead for a few seconds, then fights back.

creatures.name: Tree Frog
creatures.habitat: Shores of the Misty Lake and the Bamboo Forest of the Lost; by day and at night in spring and summer, in rain as well.
creatures.description: A frog as bright green as a new leaf, with a cream belly, that hops about near water and among the bamboo. It is harmless.

creatures.name: Tsuchinoko
creatures.habitat: Fields and hills of the plains and Youkai Mountain; by day in summer. Very rare.
creatures.description: The legendary tsuchinoko: a short snake, fat in the middle, earth-brown with dark bands. It is very shy, and once seen it bites its own tail and rolls away like a hoop.

creatures.name: Pond Turtle
creatures.habitat: Shore of the Misty Lake; by day in spring and summer. At the shrine: sunning itself on the bank of the pond past the bridge.
creatures.description: A pond turtle with an olive shell and a yellow cheek stripe that loves to sun itself on a stone. It doesn't run from anyone: it pulls into its shell until they leave.

creatures.name: White Snake
creatures.habitat: Hills of Youkai Mountain and the Hill of the Shrine; by day in spring and summer. At the shrine: now and then coiled in the courtyard by the hall. Rare.
creatures.description: A sacred white snake with a red eye that suns itself coiled near the altars. It flees from no one and never attacks.

creatures.name: Will-o'-the-Wisp
creatures.habitat: Shore and waters of the Misty Lake; only at dawn, all year, in rain as well. At the shrine: over the pond at dawn.
creatures.description: A pale green flame that glows over the water when the mist rises at dawn. It fights back only if provoked.

creatures.name: Wolf Tengu
creatures.habitat: Hills and peaks of Youkai Mountain; by day and at night, all year, in snow as well. Never on the shrine grounds.
creatures.description: A white-haired tengu guard with wolf ears, a full tail, a dark dress and a straight sword. She stands at her post and drives off anyone who comes near the mountain.

races.name: Amanojaku
traits: Bad status effects turn around in your favour
Weak to spirit damage, resists physical
races.blurb: A contrary youkai that turns anything the other way round, for those who would rather be hated by choice than tolerated out of pity.

races.name: Animal spirit
traits: Gains the gift of the clan you join
Sees trails of scent and in the dark
races.blurb: A spirit of the Animal Realm who has proven its strength and walks with a pack that hunts together and asks no questions.

races.name: Baku
races.blurb: The dream-eater who tends the Dream World, for those who would rather guard the sleep of others than fight awake.

races.name: Boundary youkai
traits: Opens gaps: reaches chests from afar and catches your falls
Sleeps half the day and all winter
Mending the barrier becomes your duty
races.blurb: The strongest race in the game and the longest route: the youkai who decides where one thing ends and the next begins.

races.name: Celestial
traits: An envoy comes for you every year
races.blurb: A body forged of heavenly peaches that no knife pierces, for those who want to stand above it all.

races.name: Youkai of darkness
traits: Wraps itself in a sphere of night, even at noon
races.blurb: The thing that waits outside the ring of torchlight, for those who choose to stop fearing the dark by becoming it.

races.name: Divine spirit
traits: Never hungry and does not age
Sees the wish of each person
Its grave must not be found
races.blurb: A hero who fell for others and returns as a worshipped spirit: a death that is not the end.

races.name: Doll
traits: Feels no pain and ignores spores and miasma
races.blurb: A body of cloth and porcelain that feels no pain and can always be sewn back together, paid for in size.

races.name: Dragon
traits: Flies, and breathes and swims in water
Its pearl can break or be stolen
races.blurb: The highest god of Gensokyo, whose seat has stood empty since the Barrier was made: the goal of a whole save.

races.name: Enenra
traits: Slips through gaps, grates and chimneys
Takes no fall damage and does not breathe
Loses its traits when soaked; wind scatters it
races.blurb: Smoke from a campfire that takes a face, which nothing can hold, cut or shut out.

races.name: Fairy
traits: A body only 1 block tall with low flight
races.blurb: The weakest race in the game and the only one whose character is never lost to a mistake: a fairy falls and comes back.

races.name: Firefly youkai
traits: Has a light of its own; insects do not attack
races.blurb: A light that never walks in the dark or alone, for those who would rather tend a garden than carry a sword.

races.name: Flower youkai
traits: Open flowers make it stronger; hostile plants spare it
races.blurb: One of the strongest beings in Gensokyo, who wants no throne, only a field no one dares to step on.

races.name: Funayuurei
traits: Breathes and swims in water; sees in the dark underwater
A bottomless ladle cancels its power
races.blurb: The drowned one who became mistress of the lake and never drowns again.

races.name: Ghost
traits: Its grave must not be found
races.blurb: One of the dead who stays out of attachment, given the time that was missing to keep a promise.

races.name: Were-hakutaku
traits: Reads an enemy's weakness and next blow
Takes a horned form at the full moon
Answers the call of the Village
races.blurb: The beast that humans trust: it teaches by day, guards the Village by night, and can erase what should never have happened.

races.name: Half-phantom
traits: Chills the air and does not age
races.blurb: Half of the beyond without letting go of life: a faster sword and a second body that goes where the first cannot.

races.name: Half-youkai
traits: Does not age and never gets sick
Youkai do not attack it and humans do not fear it
races.blurb: The only one youkai leave alone and humans do not fear: weak of arm, and free to pass between both worlds.

races.name: Haniwa
traits: Feels no pain and knows no fear
Stronger near its lord, weaker without one
races.blurb: A clay soldier made to stand at someone's side forever, without having to die for it.

races.name: Hashihime
traits: Sees jealousy and fondness in others
races.blurb: The guardian of bridges who feeds on jealousy, for those who keep the hurt instead of healing it and find power in it.

races.name: Hell raven
traits: Immune to fire and heat, with a light of its own
races.blurb: A raven that carries fire in its body and may one day swallow a sun, at the cost of being welcome almost nowhere.

races.name: Hermit
traits: Does not age and falls slowly, unharmed
Carries a pocket home, the Senkai
Two sutras a day, or no Energy
An envoy from Hell comes for you every year
races.blurb: A human who lives for centuries, barely eats and carries a home behind a paper door, trading the feast for peace.

races.name: Hourai immortal
traits: Immune to sickness and poison; does not age
Feels the pain of every return
Can be sealed away while down
races.blurb: Whoever drinks the elixir no longer dies of blade, fire or sickness, and has yet to learn what staying forever means.

races.name: Human
traits: The starting race; its forms never spend your one change
Welcome everywhere and the only one who can still go home
Can sign the contract of the Village
Without the contract, youkai may hunt you as prey
races.blurb: Where everyone starts: a human who stays human learns every craft, is welcome everywhere, and can still go home.

races.name: Inchling
traits: Unseen in tall grass; a 1-block hole is a burrow
Youkai may hunt you as prey
races.blurb: A thumb-sized person who fits in a crack, lives inside a wall and travels on a friend's shoulder.

races.name: Jiangshi
traits: Feels no pain and does not breathe
races.blurb: A tireless risen corpse that takes a blow without blinking, eats anything and works all night.

races.name: Kami
traits: Steps between its torii gates and flies
Returns from death, paid for in Faith
No Energy without a shrine nearby
races.blurb: A god made of faith alone, for those who want to belong to a place so much that they become it.

races.name: Kappa
traits: Carries a workbench in its backpack
The dish on its head must stay wet
races.blurb: A river engineer with clever hands, for the outsider who misses machines and would rather mend the world than fight it.

races.name: Kasha
traits: Has a beast form and a cart that follows it
Kept away by salt and houses in mourning
races.blurb: The cat who comes after death, hears what the dead still have to say and carries them to the end of the road.

races.name: Fox youkai
traits: Its true name holds power over it
races.blurb: A fox that wins without fighting: it knows more, reckons first and wears whichever face suits.

races.name: Komainu
traits: Has a post of its own and sees in the dark
races.blurb: A stone lion-dog that guards a place of worship, for those who found a home and never want to leave it.

races.name: Living god
traits: Keeps the contract of the Village
races.blurb: The power of a god without ceasing to be a person, for those who want to be needed rather than feared.

races.name: Lunarian
races.blurb: A noble of the Moon who left the round of eating, killing and rotting behind, and must never dirty their hands again.

races.name: Magician
traits: Stops aging in its last form
races.blurb: A scholar who trades hunger for research and, in time, old age itself: the only youkai route the Village puts up with.

races.name: Mermaid
traits: Breathes and swims in water, and is stronger there
races.blurb: Peace and a home no one can reach, at the price of your legs.

races.name: Misfortune god
traits: Those who stay near catch Bad Luck
races.blurb: A goddess who gathers the bad luck of humans and keeps it, knowing no one will be able to stay close.

races.name: Moon rabbit
traits: Joins the rabbits' network, which speaks at any distance
Killing with a blade costs an orb
races.blurb: A soldier of the Moon with a post, a uniform and a thousand voices at its side, who may desert at the risk of being hunted.

races.name: Mouse youkai
traits: Sounding is free and names every ore, chest and hollow nearby
Has a beast form and sees in the dark
races.blurb: The temple mouse who finds what was lost, for those who would rather know where things are than be strong.

races.name: Nekomata
traits: Takes no fall damage and clings to walls
Has a cat form; three cats follow it
Swims badly and loses its traits when soaked
races.blurb: A cat walks into any yard and sleeps on any roof, and nobody asks whose it is.

races.name: Night sparrow
traits: Sees in the dark, glides and flies low
Goes hoarse when wet or frozen
races.blurb: A singer of the night road with a food stall under a red lantern, serving humans and youkai alike.

races.name: Nue
traits: Each people sees it as one of their own
races.blurb: A creature no one can identify, which enters anywhere as no one, for those who accept that hardly anyone will truly know them.

races.name: Nyuudou companion
traits: Breaks blocks by hand; flies in its last form
The cloud vanishes when seen whole
races.blurb: Face the giant cloud of the mountain road without running, and you gain a friend who never leaves.

races.name: Oni
traits: Cannot lie and refuses no challenge
races.blurb: Monstrous strength, two horns and a word that always holds, for those who never again want to run, deceive or ask leave.

races.name: Phantom
traits: Passes through walls and hovers, never falling
A thin voice: short answers only
races.blurb: The safety net of a world where dying is final: after a week of preparation, the first death is no longer the end.

races.name: Poltergeist
traits: Hovers and never falls; a stage counts as its post
races.blurb: The noise that stays when the owner is gone: the house becomes your body and everything in it obeys.

races.name: Poverty and pestilence god
traits: Sees chests and gold through walls
Those who stay near grow poor
races.blurb: A god who turns want into a weapon: whoever stays near grows poor, and what was theirs runs into your hand.

races.name: Rokurokubi
traits: Passes for human; a neck that stretches
Its head can fly off as a second body
The head wanders while you sleep
races.blurb: A youkai who lives among humans unnoticed: human by day, a flying head over the Village by night.

races.name: Saint
traits: Reads wishes and the next blow
Three wishes heard a day, or no Faith
An envoy comes for you every year
races.blurb: One who hears ten people at once and knows what each wishes, ending quarrels at the cost of their own peace.

races.name: Satori
traits: Reads wishes and the next blow through the third eye
races.blurb: A mind-reader no one can lie to or ambush, and whom almost no one wants nearby.

races.name: Season god
traits: Garden beds grow out of season
races.blurb: A harvest god called every year to bless the fields, for those who would rather be loved than feared.

races.name: Shinigami
traits: Sees exactly how much Life everyone has
Calls the ferry on deep water
The living read it as an omen
races.blurb: The ferrier of the Sanzu River, who tends the passage of the dead with a boat, a superior and a quota.

races.name: Bake-danuki
traits: Pays weekly dues to the band
races.blurb: A shapeshifting raccoon dog with a loud, generous family, for those who would rather fool the world than be beaten by it.

races.name: Tengu
traits: Flies faster and more cheaply than others
Gains the gift of its caste
Bound by the law of the mountain
races.blurb: The fastest flier in the sky and first to every story, with a place in an order that commands it.

races.name: Tiger youkai
traits: Has a beast form that fights
Carries a pagoda relic that can be lost
races.blurb: The beast a god chose: strong, rich, feared by the wicked and loved by the weak.

races.name: Tsuchigumo
traits: Walks on walls and ceilings and places web by hand
races.blurb: An earth spider that never falls, weaves its own bridges and belongs to the cheerful folk underground.

races.name: Tsukumogami
traits: Becomes one with a cherished object and can turn into it
races.blurb: A thrown-away thing that refused to end, become one with the object you cherished most.

races.name: Vampire
traits: Sees in the dark, heals itself, glides and later flies
races.blurb: A night without end and a seat at the table of the Mansion of the Lake, paid for with the day itself.

races.name: Werewolf
traits: Sees trails of scent and in the dark
Forced into wolf form at the full moon
races.blurb: A person by day and a hunter by night, who keeps the life it has and gains the teeth it lacked.

races.name: Yama
traits: Cannot lie and accepts no gifts or favourites
races.blurb: The judge with the last word on every life, for those who accept becoming roadside stone first.

races.name: Yamabiko
traits: An echo floats nearby as a second body
Goes hoarse when wet or frozen
races.blurb: The youkai of the mountain echo, who makes sure every cheerful voice gets a reply.

races.name: Yamanba
traits: Has a sanctuary of its own
races.blurb: The mistress of the wild who lives alone on the mountain, on ground no one can take.

races.name: Yamawaro
traits: Unseen when standing still in the woods
races.blurb: A trader who deals with everyone and belongs to no one, for those who want freedom and a full purse.

races.name: Youkai of dread
traits: Sees in the dark and heals itself
Its true name holds power over it
races.blurb: A tale well told that outlasts any body: stop being prey and become the reason nobody goes out at night.

races.name: Youkai rabbit
traits: Has a Luck gauge and escapes one killing blow
Never lost in the bamboo forest; ears that warn of danger
races.blurb: A rabbit who lasts by minding her health and her luck, wanting only to be alive next year and see others safely home.

races.name: Yuki-onna
traits: The cold never hurts it; it chills the air around
races.blurb: The youkai of winter, reached the way the folklore says: die of cold in the snow and stand up again.

races.name: Zashiki-warashi
traits: Hears every room of the house
Away too long, the house declines
races.blurb: The spirit that lives in a house and makes it prosper, for those who want a home more than strength.

race_rules: Every new life begins as a human outsider. The human line has three forms of its own (Outsider, Human of Gensokyo, Human Hero), and reaching them never spends your change.
You can change race only once per life. Holding a race's rite spends that change, crosses out every other page in the Book of Races, and there is no way back.
Every race grows through three forms. Each form changes how you look and, outside the human line, raises your Attack and Life. Once you reach a form you never leave it.
A route for the living always ends in a rite: the right place, the right hour and someone to lead it. You confirm by holding the button for 3 seconds, and a transformation cutscene plays.
Races are not balanced. Each has a grade from 1 to 5 (Small, Common, Strong, Great, Legendary), and the stronger the race, the longer its route and the higher its price. The human line has no grade.
Some routes ask for your death, and the Book marks them with a skull. If you die exactly the way the route asks, you can hold the button to come back as that race; refusing ends that life.
Press Y to open the Book of Races. It shows every race's requirements and your progress, and you can pin one race as your goal.
Death is permanent. If your Life reaches zero outside a Spell Card duel, the save ends and becomes a memorial with a tombstone that tells your story.

stations.name: By hand
stations.purpose: Crafting with bare hands, anywhere, opened with B. Makes Fiber Rope, Torches, the first Axe, the Campfire, the Carpenter's Table, Red Cord and the eight elemental crystals.

stations.name: Campfire
stations.purpose: The first cooking fire (1x1 cell). Roasts fish, burns fuel while it works, stops in rain when uncovered, and gives light for 3 cells while lit. A Campfire is also an ingredient of the Kamado.

stations.name: Carpenter's Table
stations.purpose: The main workbench (3x2 cells). Makes tools, wooden and bamboo blocks, furniture, chests, bench upgrades, the other benches, ammunition and every copper weapon. It only makes progress while you stand within 4 cells of it.

stations.name: Kamado
stations.purpose: The clay cooking stove (3x2 cells), made with a Campfire. Cooks Onigiri, Green Tea, Miso Soup and Rice with Mushroom, and also makes Washi and Vermilion Ink. It burns fuel, stops in rain when uncovered, and gives light for 4 cells while lit. Planned: a cook helper working it for you.

stations.name: Clay Oven
stations.purpose: A tall clay oven (2x3 cells) for firing Clay Bricks and Roof Tiles, smelting Copper Ingots and making Gunpowder. With a Charcoal Mouth beside it (level 2) it smelts Iron into Iron Bloom and Gold into Gold Ingots. Each firing takes fuel, it stops in rain when uncovered, and it gives light for 3 cells while lit.

stations.name: Charcoal Kiln
stations.purpose: A mound of earth over stacked wood (3x3 cells) that turns 10 Wood into 6 Charcoal over 4 game hours. It needs no tending and the rain does not stop it. Its queue holds 4 jobs.

stations.name: Anvil
stations.purpose: The smithing anvil (2x2 cells). Makes Iron Ingots, iron tools, Steel Ingots, the Master Pickaxe and Cut Diamonds, plus every iron, gold and diamond weapon. Iron weapons need level 2, gold level 3, and diamond weapons and Steel Ingots level 4. It only makes progress while you stand within 4 cells of it.

stations.name: Ofuda Desk
stations.purpose: Planned: a desk for writing ofuda talismans and charms with washi and ink. The bench and its recipes are not in the game yet. Vermilion Ink is boiled at the Kamado for now.
