craft_how: Opening the window: press B to craft with your bare hands, anywhere. To use a bench, point at it while it is within reach (it gets a gold outline) and right-click it. Esc closes the window, Enter makes the selected recipe, and Tab moves between categories. The world keeps running while the window is open, so benches keep working and time keeps passing.

The window: the bench is shown at the top left, with its name and level on the signboard. Below that are category tabs (Everything, Tools, Weapons, Blocks, Furniture, Chests, Upgrades, Benches, Food, Parts), and each bench only shows the tabs it uses. There are three filters: 'I can make it', 'One thing short' and 'All'. Every recipe in the list has a mark showing whether you can make it now, are missing materials, need a better bench, or have not learnt it yet. The detail panel shows the result, how many of each ingredient you have against how many you need, where each one comes from (your hands, a nearby chest or fuel), the time in minutes, and what quality the item will come out at.
Time: all crafting times are in game minutes. At normal game speed, one game minute passes in one real second.

Learning recipes: recipes start hidden. The first time you pick up a material, every recipe that uses it appears as a dark silhouette marked 'Not learnt yet'. Once you have held all of a recipe's ingredients, you learn it. Some recipes also wait for one more item: for example, the Bamboo Bow and Arrows are only learnt once you have also picked up Copper, and the Water Tub and Whetstone once you have held an Anvil. Green Tea is taught by the Shrine Maiden when your relationship with her reaches Friend.

Batches: choose x1, x5 or Max before pressing Make. Max makes as many as your materials allow, up to 5 at the start, plus 1 for every 5 levels of Crafting, to a limit of 15. Each bench queues up to 8 jobs (the Charcoal Kiln queues 4). The tray along the bottom shows what is being worked on, what is waiting and why, and what is ready.

Where materials come from: a bench with no linked chests uses what you carry and what is stored in chests within 12 cells of it. Crafting by hand reaches chests within 12 cells of you. Chests marked private are never used.

Linked chests: a placed bench has a second page, Link chest. There you can choose a Materials chest, which supplies the ingredients, and a Production chest, which receives everything the bench makes. Only a chest touching the bench's left or right side can be linked, and private chests cannot be linked. With a Materials chest linked, recipes take ingredients only from that chest. With a Production chest linked, finished items go only into that chest. If the Production chest is full, the bench shows 'Production chest is full.' and waits. If a linked chest is moved or broken, the bench shows 'Chest disconnected.' and stops until you link a chest again or remove the link. While you point at a bench, its links are drawn in the world, labelled Materials and Production.

How benches work: crafting by hand always makes progress, wherever you are. The Carpenter's Table and the Anvil only make progress while you stand within 4 cells of them, and what they make goes straight to your hands. The fire benches (Campfire, Kamado and Clay Oven) keep cooking or firing on their own once loaded, and the Charcoal Kiln smoulders by itself. Items finished on their own wait on the bench, shown resting on it with a glint, until you take them from the window's tray. A linked Production chest receives finished items in either case. Planned: helpers who can work a bench for you.

Fuel: the Campfire and the Kamado burn one minute of fire for every minute of work. A piece of Wood lasts 20 minutes, a Twig 5 minutes and a piece of Charcoal 60 minutes. Each Clay Oven firing costs 20 minutes of fire: one Wood, four Twigs or one Charcoal.

Rain: the Campfire, Kamado and Clay Oven stop in rain or snow if they stand outdoors with no block above them. The Carpenter's Table, Anvil and Charcoal Kiln are not affected. A stopped bench shows a bubble with the reason it is waiting: rain, a missing ingredient (shown by its icon), or nobody working it.

Quality: crafted items come out Common, Fine or Masterwork. Quality is never random. It is a sum of points shown before you craft. Material: +1 for each tier by which the material you choose for a flexible ingredient (such as 'any Wood') is above the recipe's tier, up to +2. Bench gives +1 for each level above the level the recipe needs, up to +3. Your skill gives +1 for every 10 levels above five times the recipe's tier, up to +3. 0 to 2 points makes Common, 3 to 5 makes Fine, and 6 or more makes Masterwork. Only single items (tools, weapons, furniture), food and harvested crops can have a quality. Blocks, benches and parts are always Common. Items remember who made them ('Made by ...'). A Fine item is worth 1.5x and a Masterwork 2x. Planned: a specialist helper adding +1, and Fine and Masterwork food lasting 1.25x and 1.5x as long once eating arrives.

Bench upgrades: a bench's level is 1, plus 1 for each different upgrade of its own placed within 6 cells of it, up to level 4. Some recipes need a higher bench level. Carpenter's Table: Jig Shelf, Bow Saw (the Plane is planned). Kamado: Bamboo Steamer (more planned). Clay Oven: Charcoal Mouth (more planned). Anvil: Water Tub, Whetstone, Forge Bellows. Iron weapons need Anvil level 2, gold weapons level 3, and diamond weapons and Steel Ingots level 4. The Master Pickaxe needs level 3 and Cut Diamond level 2.

Placing benches: benches and upgrades are items. Select one in the hotbar and right-click to set it down on solid ground within reach. Hold left-click on a bench to pick it back up. A bench that is working, or that holds finished items, stays where it is until you empty it. Benches can be set down outdoors, around the shrine (outside its protected grounds) and in the fields of the world map, but not inside rooms.

Extra materials from gathering: felling a tree (not bamboo or a giant mushroom) gives 2 Twigs, and every third tree also gives a piece of Mulberry Bark. Every third Dirt block you dig gives Clay, and every third Iron block you mine gives Cinnabar.
farming: Planned (not playable yet): crops by season, with days until harvest. Spring: Tea (10 days, then picks again every 5 days; Tea Seeds), Soybean (8; Soybean Seeds), Turnip (5; Turnip Seeds). Summer: Rice (12; Rice Seed; needs shallow water in its cell), Cucumber (6; Cucumber Seed), Eggplant (7; Eggplant Seed). Autumn: Sweet Potato (8; Sweet Potato Slip), Pumpkin (9; Pumpkin Seed), Mushroom (6; Mushroom Log). Winter: Daikon (7; Daikon Seed), Chard (8; Chard Seed).
Fairies sometimes drop a plain Seed with no crop of its own. Planned: once sown, it grows a crop of the current season that suits the bed, and harvesting it gives back that crop's own seed.
The Stone Hoe and the Bamboo Watering Can can already be made at the Carpenter's Table. Planned: digging dirt or grass into a bed with the hoe and watering beds with the can.

Planned (not playable yet): dig a bed with the hoe and sow seeds only in their season. Water each bed once a day, and rain does the watering for you. A day without water does not count towards growth, but the plant never dies. A ripe crop gives 1 produce, 2 from Farming level 20 and 3 from level 40, always plus one seed back. Tea keeps producing after its first harvest.

Cooking today: the Campfire roasts Grilled Fish, and the Kamado cooks Onigiri, Green Tea, Miso Soup and Rice with Mushroom (the last needs a level 2 Kamado, for example with a Bamboo Steamer beside it). Both burn fuel while cooking and stop in rain when uncovered. Dishes can come out Fine or Masterwork.

Dish stats (eating is planned): Grilled Fish gives 20 sustenance and 10 health per hour for 120 minutes. Onigiri gives 25 sustenance and 10 health per hour for 180 minutes, plus Travel affinity. Green Tea gives 5 sustenance for 240 minutes, plus Rite affinity. Miso Soup gives 30 sustenance and 20 health per hour for 240 minutes, plus Farming affinity. Rice with Mushroom gives 45 sustenance and 20 health per hour for 360 minutes, plus a +3% food bonus. An affinity gives +10% in that skill until the end of the day.

Planned (not playable yet): you can have three different dishes active at once, each with its own timer, and you cannot stack the same dish twice. Fine dishes last 1.25x as long and Masterwork dishes 1.5x.

places.name: Hakurei Shrine
places.description: Home of the Shrine Maiden, on the Great Barrier at the far eastern edge of Gensokyo. Every journey starts here, and no hostile encounters happen within two tiles of it.

places.name: Hill of the Shrine
places.description: The wooded hill around the Hakurei Shrine, the gentlest ground on the map.

places.name: Trail of the Shrine
places.description: The dirt trail that runs west from the shrine to the Human Village. Roads are the safest and quickest way to travel.

places.name: Human Village
places.description: The heart of Gensokyo and the outsider's refuge. No hostile encounters happen next to it. Its gates do not open to you yet.

places.name: Myouren Temple
places.description: A temple just south-east of the Human Village.

places.name: Temple Cemetery
places.description: The graveyard beside the Myouren Temple.

places.name: Road of the Temple
places.description: The road from the Village past the Myouren Temple, south to the edge of the bamboo forest.

places.name: Kourindou
places.description: A curio shop at the edge of the Forest of Magic, on the road out of the Village.

places.name: Road of the Forest
places.description: A short road from the Human Village west to Kourindou.

places.name: Road of the Lake
places.description: The road north from the Village, then west to the southern shore of the Misty Lake.

places.name: Misty Lake
places.description: A lake at the foot of the mountain. Its mist cuts your sight on the map to one tile. The water freezes in winter, and then you can walk across it.

places.name: Mansion of the Lake
places.description: A red mansion on the northern shore of the Misty Lake.

places.name: Forest of Magic
places.description: A dark forest of beeches and giant mushrooms west of the Human Village, thick with smaller mushrooms and ferns.

places.name: House in the Woods
places.description: A lone house in the south of the Forest of Magic.

places.name: Cottage of the Dolls
places.description: A cottage in the north of the Forest of Magic.

places.name: Forest of the Tanuki
places.description: A wood of beeches and pines south of the Forest of Magic, watched over by little tanuki statues. The grove at its heart cannot be entered yet.

places.name: Bamboo Forest of the Lost
places.description: A maze of bamboo in the south-east. On the map it turns you around about one step in three unless a guide shows the way.

places.name: Eientei
places.description: A manor hidden deep in the Bamboo Forest of the Lost. Only a guide knows the way.

places.name: Garden of the Sun
places.description: Fields of sunflowers in a basin in the far south. They come alive only in summer.

places.name: Nameless Hill
places.description: A hill of lilies of the valley in the far south. The flowers are poisonous.

places.name: Mayohiga
places.description: An abandoned village in the far north, near the Great Barrier.

places.name: Youkai Mountain
places.description: The only mountain inside Gensokyo, in the north-west. Its slopes and foothills can be explored, but the tengu guard the high peaks.

places.name: Climb of the Mountain
places.description: The path up Youkai Mountain, past the forest, the kappa valley, the waterfall and the tengu village to the summit.

places.name: Great Youkai Forest
places.description: A small, dense wood on the first stretch of the mountain climb.

places.name: Kappa Valley
places.description: The kappa's workshop valley on the mountain river.

places.name: Geyser Center
places.description: A kappa facility at the foot of the mountain, built over the geyser.

places.name: Falls of the Nine Heavens
places.description: The great waterfall halfway up Youkai Mountain.

places.name: Tengu Village

seasons: A year has 120 days: four months of 30 days each, named after their seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter.
The week has seven days. A new game starts on Monday, Spring 1 of Year 1. Summer starts on a Wednesday, Autumn on a Friday, Winter on a Sunday, and Year 2 starts on a Tuesday.
Time runs at one game minute per real second, so a full day takes 24 real minutes. A new game starts at 07:00.
On the world map, the clock moves only when you take a step, wait (10 minutes) or camp. Each step costs from 5 minutes on a road to 30 minutes on a high mountain.

The day plate in the corner of the screen shows the sun or moon crossing the sky, the weekday and day of the month, the time in 10-minute steps, and icons for the season and the weather. Its calendar button (or C) opens the wall calendar.
On the first day of each season, a painted scroll unrolls across the top of the screen with the season's name and landscape.
Sunrise and sunset by season: Spring 05:30 to 18:30, Summer 04:30 to 19:30, Autumn 06:30 to 17:30, Winter 07:30 to 16:30.
Weather is rolled for every six-hour block. Chance of rain: Spring 25%, Summer 40%, Autumn 30%. In Winter, the 30% chance brings snow instead of rain.

The first day of every Spring is always clear. About 40% of spring days are petal days, and Spring 1 always is one: on those days cherry petals drift down near the cherry trees while the sky is clear.
Rain makes each step on the world map take 20% longer, and snow 40% longer.
Snow piles up on open ground while it falls, up to a thin layer, and keeps footprints. A clear winter day keeps the snow, and it melts once Winter ends. Snow does not water plants.
In Winter, ponds, lakes and the water under bridges freeze over and can be walked on. On the world map, frozen lakes can be crossed on foot.
Wild plants rest in Winter and weeds stop growing. In the shrine garden, weeds grow faster in Summer and slower in Autumn, and fallen leaves pile up most in Autumn.
Trees, plants, ground, the sky and the distant landscape all change with the season: blossoms in Spring, deep green in Summer, red and gold in Autumn, snow in Winter.
The moon crosses the night sky in eight phases over the month. It is new on day 30 and full on day 15.
The sky has its own colours for dawn, day, dusk and night. Clouds drift with the game clock, stars twinkle at night, and rain or snow turns the sky grey and hides the sun.

peoples: The Hakurei Shrine (tier 0): the Shrine Maiden's home at the eastern edge of Gensokyo. It offers a home and rites.
The Human Village (tier 1): trade, seeds, household recipes and protection.
Kourindou (tier 2): the curio shop at the forest's edge, selling objects from the outside world.
The Myouren Temple (tier 2): near the Village, a refuge for youkai.
The Mansion of the Lake (tier 3): at the Misty Lake. Library, blood and martial arts.
The Witches of the Forest (tier 4): in the Forest of Magic. Cauldron, magic and grimoires.
Eientei (tier 4): hidden in the Bamboo Forest of the Lost. Medicines and the moon.
The Kappa (tier 5): in the mountain's valley. Machines, parts and an elevator.
The Tengu (tier 5): high on the mountain. The mountain pass, the newspaper and the wind.
The Moriya Shrine (tier 5): at the summit. Faith, gods and technology.
The Oni below (tier 6): in the Former Hell. Forge, strength and sake.
The Netherworld (tier 7): above the clouds. Swordplay and the dead.
Heaven (tier 7): above the mountain. Celestial peaches and keystones.
Apart from the Hakurei Shrine, the homes of the peoples cannot be visited yet.

Favor: each people has a favor track from 0 to 5. On the world map, favor is the only thing that can keep you out of a named place: places of tier 2 ask favor 1 with the Village, tier 3 favor 1 with the Mansion, tier 4 favor 1 with the Witches of the Forest, tier 5 favor 2 with the Kappa, tier 6 favor 1 with the Oni, and tier 7 favor 1 with the Netherworld or Heaven. Planned ways to raise it are fair trade, the people's own tasks, gifts and settling incidents in their lands; breaking their things, being a race they fear or spreading fear will lower it. Earning favor is not in the game yet.
Places with no people, such as Mayohiga, the Forest of the Tanuki, Muenzuka and the Sanzu, have no favor track.

cast.personality: Keeper of the shrine, and the one character who lives in the world today. Blunt, carefree and a little lazy, but dutiful and kind underneath. She warms up slowly, gets flustered by affection and always hopes someone left a donation. She likes tea, sweets, quiet sunny days and a compliment. She dislikes incidents, troublemakers, needless fuss, rain on the laundry and chores in the cold. Her walk is Relaxed: weight on one leg, in no hurry.

Confident and unbothered. Blonde waves under a pointed witch's hat, and a black-and-white witch's dress with an apron. She walks with a confident stride. She is one of the ready-made looks in the cast and does not live in the world yet.
Cool; he has seen it all before. Messy dark-brown hair, a charcoal hoodie, jeans and sneakers. Walks with his hands in his pockets. This is the starting look for a male player character.
Curious; what is that over there? A chestnut ponytail, green eyes, a sakura-pink hoodie, jeans and sneakers. Her walk is Curious. This is the starting look for a female player character.
Stern; you will have to win them over. Raven hair in a bun with a headband, a cream kosode and a navy hakama. Walks with a stern step. A ready-made look in the cast; not a resident of the world yet.
Cheerful and quick to wave hello. Sakura-pink twin tails with a small ribbon, violet eyes and a teal yukata. Walks Cheerful. A ready-made look in the cast; not a resident of the world yet.

Thoughtful, always turning a question over. Long silver hair in a hime cut, amber eyes, a wisteria traveler's shirt and vest, and a travel pack. Walks Thoughtful. A ready-made look in the cast; not a resident of the world yet.

life_facts: The Shrine Maiden keeps a full daily routine that shifts with the hour, the weather and how tired she is, so no two days play out quite the same.

Morning: she wakes on her futon between 5:30 and 6:40, folds it away, bathes on most days, changes out of her sleepwear and almost always prays first thing. On clear mornings she may stretch or air out her room. She cooks breakfast between 6:40 and 9:30. Then come tea, tending the altar, checking the offerings, writing and placing ofuda, and sometimes a purification rite.
Midday: she sweeps the grounds (or the floors when it rains), tends the garden, tidies the altar and her room, and has lunch between 11:30 and 13:15.

Afternoon: tea, sweeping, reading and feeding the koi on clear days. She naps only when she is tired. With the right furniture in her room she also studies scrolls, sews on rainy days and warms up by the brazier.

Sunset and night: she watches the sky, drinks tea, lights the lanterns on clear evenings and has dinner between 18:30 and 20:30. Between 21:00 and 23:00 she says a short prayer at the altar, closes the window, lays out her futon and goes to bed.

Interruptions: when it rains she goes to close the window. When a visitor arrives she comes to greet them, but never while she is sleeping, bathing, changing or praying. During an incident she drops everything to investigate.
She waves when you first come near and waves goodbye when you part. She can't chat while she is asleep, in the bath, changing or praying.

Shared activities: Have tea together, Tea by the brazier together, Sit together, Walk together, Walk hand in hand, Sweep together, Tend the grounds together, Cook together, Eat together, Read together, Pray together, Feed the koi together and Investigate together. The two walks, feeding the koi and investigating need a clear day. Each activity raises your bond a little, but the gain shrinks if you repeat it too often within a few days.

Special moments: some shared activities mean more at the right time. Examples: sitting together at sunset, tea in the rain, a quiet walk in the morning or at sunset, dinner together at night, feeding the koi at sunset and reading together while it rains.

She takes the initiative too. Once you are friends she may invite you to join her tea, tea by the brazier, meal, reading, koi feeding or prayer, and she may pay you a compliment. Once you are best friends (or she is smitten), she may run up for a hug when you come back after most of a day away, or invite you to watch the sunset together. She does this at most three times a day.

Talking: start a conversation with Greet her. How she greets you depends on your bond, the time of day, her mood, how long you were away and what she remembers. Then choose what to say: Make small talk, How are you?, Ask about her, Tell her about your day, Tease her, Praise her work, Offer to help, Talk about donations and Say goodbye. Remember together appears once you know each other and share memories, and Speak tenderly once you are friends. Apologize and Comfort her appear when they make sense.

Each thing you say can go well, neutral or badly, depending on your bond, her mood and what she is doing. Teasing a stranger goes badly, but between friends it lands well. She is used to doing everything alone, so offers of help take time to be welcome. Say the same thing too often in one day and she will point out that you are repeating yourself.
She asks questions of her own, more often the closer you are. An answer that suits her pleases her, one that goes against her annoys her, and she remembers what you said.
Her patience runs out. Every line costs some, she recovers one point every 40 minutes of game time, and when it is gone she ends the conversation in her own way.
All speech appears in balloons over the speaker's head. Her portrait and current emotion show on the interaction card.

Emotions: joy, affection, shyness, surprise, annoyance, anger, sadness, tiredness, smugness and worry. They show on her face, in her portrait and as icons over her head, then slowly settle back to her usual mood.

Memory: she remembers what happens. Trivial things fade within a couple of hours; the biggest moments, such as your first meeting or a confession, are never forgotten. She knows why she feels the way she does: if you upset her you can apologize, and if something else upset her you can comfort her.

Emotes (T key): opens the Emotes menu with your poses, including Small wave, Open arms, Bow, Salute, Prayer, Hand on heart, Cheer, Fist raised, Shrug, Scratching head, Pointing and Finger to lips. Its Do something section lets you Sit here, Look into the distance, Stretch or Sweep here.

Gestures with her are in the Gestures tab of her interaction window, for example Compliment, Pat on the head, Hug, Hold hands, Show interest, Forehead touch and Confess your feelings. Follow me is under Orders. A gesture plays out in stages (approaching, start, the moment, ending) at a speed from 0.5x to 2x, and ending it early takes you smoothly to the final stage. A gesture she isn't ready for can still be tried: she reacts in her own way, and nothing is ever forced.
relationships: Three bars measure your bond with her. Favor is general good will: it rises with help on chores and with tea, and falls when you get in her way or keep insisting. Trust is built by constancy: coming back on different days, helping without being asked, respecting a refusal and joining an investigation raise it, while insisting after a no or waking her lowers it. Intimacy is the comfort of time spent together: quiet shared activities and accepted gestures raise it, and it slowly fades after more than a week apart.
How she sees you grows from Stranger to Just met and Acquaintance, then on through the milestones of friendship and romance.

Friendship: needs 20 Favor, 15 Trust, three days spent together and two different kinds of shared activity. It unlocks Compliment, Pat on the head, Follow me and Show interest, her invitations, and one favour a day.

Best friendship: comes after Friendship and needs 40 Favor, 50 Trust, 45 Intimacy, ten days together and three kinds of shared activity. It unlocks Hug and Hold hands. Best friendship never requires romance and never leads to it on its own.
Romance is a separate path that only opens when you choose it: use Show interest, and she has to accept. You can close it at any time with Stay friends, at no cost, and the friendship stays as it is.

Yearning: needs Friendship and an open romance, plus 35 Favor, 30 Trust, 35 Intimacy and romantic moments of two different kinds on two different days. It unlocks gentle gestures such as Forehead touch and Confess your feelings, and also Hug and Hold hands.
Love: comes after Yearning and needs 60 Favor, 55 Trust, 60 Intimacy and an accepted confession.
There is also a secret final milestone, hidden from every menu until you reach it. It asks for a long, varied life together after both best friendship and love.

Respect matters. Insisting after a refusal costs Trust, and insisting twice within a week makes her ask for some room, which pauses gestures for a week. If Trust or Favor falls too low after you reach Love, the relationship becomes strained and romantic gestures pause until it mends.
Planned: leaving an offering at the shrine will raise Favor, and she already has lines for days you donated, but the offering action is not in the game yet.
helpers: Once you are friends, the Shrine Maiden can help with work. Right-click her and open the Orders section, or open the Board of orders. The board has three tabs: Ask for something, Her queue and Steps of trust.
Chop a tree: she walks to the tree you point at, fells it with her axe and brings you the wood.
Mine a block: she digs out the block you point at with her pickaxe and brings you what it drops.

Put away what you carry: she stores her load in the closest house chest whose filter accepts the item and has room. If every chest is full, she hands the items to you. She never uses your private chest.
From the Helper step you can also order Gather what lies there and Bring more of this. For Bring more of this, hold an item and she fetches up to a stack of it from the house chests.

Steps of trust: as a Friend she does one favour a day (chop a tree, mine a block or put away what she carries) and works up to half an hour a day. Helper needs Friendship, 30 Trust, 25 Favor, five days together and some standing with her people. It unlocks simple orders one at a time, up to 3 hours of work a day. Best friend unlocks a queue of up to 12 orders and up to 5 hours a day. Work partner needs Best friendship, 60 Trust, 45 Favor, five days of work covering three kinds of task, and more standing with her people. It unlocks standing orders and shifts, such as keeping a chest stocked (20 items by default) from 8:00 to 18:00, for up to 7 hours a day. Steward, the last step, needs 80 Trust, 60 Favor, fifteen days of work and a week as Work partner. It raises her work time to 8 hours a day.

She keeps her own life while working. Rain, nightfall, meals, tiredness or danger can pause an order, and she tells you why. When she can't reach a target, a red X marks it. She takes festival days off.
When the relationship is low she only does favours until things mend. Insisting after she refuses costs Trust, and thanking her for her work is always welcome.
Planned: lending her tools, equipping her, setting a work area, fighting alongside you, running crafting stations, and the Steward's extra duties of running the house on her own.

mobile: On phones and tablets the game shows touch controls (a joystick and action buttons) automatically; on PC they stay off unless you set Touch controls to Always.

Fixed joystick (bottom left): left/right walk, push it past the outer ring to sprint, down drops through platforms or aims a low blow, up swims up and aims the launcher. Optional setting: push up to jump.
Big buttons on the right: Jump (hold for a higher jump) and Use (uses what is in your hand at the aim; hold to keep mining; drag it to aim up to 4 blocks around you).

Smaller buttons: Place (right-click action: place, open a chest, guard in combat mode), E (doors and roads; it lights up when there is a way in), Roll, Layer (shows the current layer), and in areas where fights can happen, Combat mode and Lock target.
Top right: Pause, Inventory, Craft and Emotes. The Calendar opens from the clock. Skills, Book of Races and Sheet of blows are buttons in the pause menu.

Tapping the world aims there and uses your item: a short tap on a person or place opens its actions, with a block in hand it places (drag to keep placing), on a block or tree it mines while your finger stays down; a still long press (0.45 s) acts as a right-click.
Every finger works on its own control, so you can walk and jump, or walk and mine, at the same time; the hotbar also accepts a second finger.
Inside menus a small Back button (bottom right) works like Esc. Double-tap an item in the inventory to use it; hold a finger on a chest slot to move one item.

Settings > Touch: Touch controls (Auto / Always / Never), Button size (75%, 100%, 125%, 150%), Opacity (20% to 100%, default 70%), Tap on world (Uses the item / Only aims), Vibration, Push up to jump, Fill the screen (on wide phones the view grows sideways to show more of the world).
All on-screen hints switch to touch wording while touch controls are on.

first_steps.title: 1. Title screen
first_steps.text: Choose New Game. Continue lists your saves (each save is its own slot), and Settings lets you change the language before you start. English is the default.

first_steps.title: 2. Create your character
first_steps.text: Enter a name (up to 24 characters), pick a gender and shape your look: way of walking, resting pose, hair and hair colour, face, eye and skin colour, outfit, clothes and their two colours. Your race is Human. Random rolls a new look; Begin starts the game.

first_steps.title: 3. Arrival
first_steps.text: A short opening shows how an outsider falls into Gensokyo (hold Enter, Space, Esc or the mouse to skip). You wake at 07:00 in the meadow at the foot of the shrine's stone stairway, with a Simple Pickaxe in slot 1 and an Axe in slot 2.

first_steps.title: 4. Up the stairway
first_steps.text: Climb the stairs, pass under the torii and follow the stone path to the shrine. Everything from the meadow to the end of the courtyard is protected and safe: no enemies appear there, and its ground, stairs and buildings cannot be dug or built on.

first_steps.title: 5. Your first blocks
first_steps.text: Away from the shrine grounds, hold the left mouse button on dirt, grass or stone within 5 blocks of you. Broken blocks drop to the ground and fly into your bag. Switch to the Axe and hold the left button on a tree: after about 2 seconds it falls away from you and leaves 5 wood and 2 twigs at its root.

first_steps.title: 6. Build something
first_steps.text: Pick a block with 1-8 or the mouse wheel and right-click to place it. Press Q to switch between the Foreground (solid blocks you walk on) and the Background (walls behind you). A front block needs a neighbouring block or a back wall to rest on; back walls can go anywhere.

first_steps.title: 7. Craft your first tools
first_steps.text: Press B to craft. By hand you can make a Carpenter's Table (10 wood, 4 stone), Torches (1 twig + 1 Plant Fiber makes 2) and a Campfire (5 stone, 3 twigs). Plant Fiber comes from harvesting wild grass. The Carpenter's Table then makes your first weapons, such as the Bamboo Spear and Bamboo Bow, and copper tools.

first_steps.title: 8. Enter the shrine
first_steps.text: Walk up to the shrine door and press E. Inside, your tools are put away: you cannot mine or build in rooms. Press E at the exit to step outside again. The offering box in the courtyard can be right-clicked for its actions.

first_steps.title: 9. Meet the Shrine Maiden
first_steps.text: The Shrine Maiden lives here and keeps her own daily routine. Right-click her outline to open Interactions, choose Talk and Greet her. Pick what to say next; she reacts to your bond, her mood and the time of day, and she may ask you questions back. When her patience runs out she ends the chat.

first_steps.title: 10. Save and continue
first_steps.text: The game saves by itself every 30 seconds, and Esc > Save and Exit saves before returning to the title. Choose Continue to come back exactly where you stopped: your digging and felled trees are still there.

mining: The world is a side view of 16-pixel blocks with two layers: the Foreground (solid blocks you stand on and collide with) and the Background (walls behind you, with no collision). Both can exist in the same cell. Press Q to switch the layer you are working on; the badge next to the hotbar shows it.

Hold the left mouse button to mine. A progress bar fills while you hold; letting go, changing target or layer, or switching item cancels it. Your reach is 5 blocks, measured from the centre of your body.
Base mining times: Dirt and Grass 0.35 s, Wood and Wood Wall 0.6 s, Stone and Stone Wall 1.25 s, Copper 1.35 s, Iron 1.7 s, Gold 2.1 s, Diamond 2.9 s. A higher Mining skill makes it faster.

Pickaxe tiers: the Simple Pickaxe breaks soil, stone, walls and Copper; Iron needs a Copper Pickaxe; Gold needs an Iron Pickaxe; Diamond needs the Master Pickaxe. An axe can also take Wood and Wood Wall blocks.
You cannot mine a back wall while a foreground block covers that cell: take the front block first.
Mined blocks drop on the ground and are pulled into your hotbar or backpack when you have room, so you never need a free slot to dig.

Ores by depth below the local surface: Copper 5-110 blocks (most common around 35), Iron 24-235 (around 125), Gold 95-365 (around 260), Diamond 225-495 (around 410). Copper also crops out near the surface.

Placing: select a block and right-click. Each block belongs to one layer (dirt cannot go on the back layer, walls cannot go in front). A foreground block needs a neighbouring block (up, down, left or right) or a back wall in the same cell; back walls need no support. You cannot place a block inside a person or a tree trunk.
Hold the right button to keep placing as you sweep the mouse. Chests, benches and torches are placed with the right button too.

The shrine grounds are protected: the courtyard, the stone stairway and its landings, the great oak, the forest storehouse and the ground under standing landmark trees cannot be mined or built on. Rooms indoors cannot be edited at all.

Trees: hold the left button on a tree with an axe. A tree takes about 2 seconds, then falls away from you and drops 5 wood and 2 twigs at its root (every third tree also gives Mulberry Bark). Bamboo and giant mushrooms give their own loot instead. A felled tree stays gone in your save.

The Action queue (L) plans work for you: add Mine or Fell trees, drag a rectangle over blocks or click trees, press Enter, then Start. Your character walks and works through the list; moving yourself, taking damage or entering combat mode pauses it, and Continue resumes. It never undoes what was already done.

Light: the surface is lit by the sky, which fades about 12 blocks into tunnels and caves. Torches, lanterns and campfires light up the dark, and a torch or Paper Lantern held in your hand lights your way. The block cursor always stays visible in the dark.
Weather: rain and snow stop at the real ground and roofs, including what you dig or build, so a roof keeps the rain off.

skills.name: Blade
skills.trained_by: Landing blows with melee weapons, gohei, fists or tools (the last blow of a chain and heavy blows count double), and defeating enemies with them.

skills.name: Shot
skills.trained_by: Landing shots with bows and firearms, and defeating enemies with them.

skills.name: Danmaku
skills.trained_by: Landing energy attacks with staffs and grimoires. Grazing bullets and capturing Spell Cards are planned.

skills.name: Guard
skills.trained_by: Rolling through a blow in time, parrying, and taking blows (up to 10 per fight count).

skills.name: Mining
skills.trained_by: Breaking natural blocks of the land: soil and back walls a little, rock more, ores and gems the most.

skills.name: Gathering
skills.trained_by: Felling trees. Gathering rare plants and fishing are planned.

skills.name: Building
skills.trained_by: Placing blocks (crafted blocks give more), placing furniture, and installing or upgrading workbenches.

skills.name: Travel
skills.trained_by: Walking new tiles of the world map, discovering places, entering new regions and resolving road encounters.

skills.name: Cooking
skills.trained_by: Cooking dishes, making tea and sharing a meal.

skills.name: Crafting
skills.trained_by: Making things at any workbench (equipment gives the most), mending clothes, and making Fine or Masterwork pieces.

skills.name: Rite
skills.trained_by: Praying at a shrine or a kamidana (once a day per place), purifying, writing ofuda and studying scrolls.

skill_rules: There is no character level: each of the 12 skills rises on its own by doing the thing it trains, from level 1 up to 50. Press K to open the Skills sheet.
Each level makes that skill's work more efficient (+1% per level up to level 30, +0.5% per level after that), for example faster mining or cutting, or more melee damage.

Experience weighs the target's tier: tougher blocks and enemies give more. The first time you do something gives a large bonus, while repeating the same thing too often in a day, or working far below your level, gives less.
Resting gives a 25% experience bonus for a while.

Level 5 milestone: each skill unlocks a new move or action. Already in the game: the Launcher and two air blows at Blade 5, the Parry at Guard 5. The others (such as Sound for Mining, Prune for Gathering, Scaffold for Building) are planned.

Every 10 levels (10, 20, 30, 40, 50) you choose one of two rules for that skill. A new choice can be swapped for free during its first two days; after that a swap costs Faith (20 at level 10, up to 100 at level 50), once a day.
After level 50, further experience turns into Faith (1,000 experience per Faith). Praying and shrine chores also give Faith.

Three attributes come from your skills, with no points to spend: Vigor (more Life) from Blade, Guard, Mining and Gathering; Breath (more stamina) from Guard, Shot, Building and Travel; Spirit (more energy orbs) from Danmaku, Rite, Cooking, Crafting and Farming.

Renown is the sum of all 12 skill levels (12 to 600). It only goes up and is never spent. Titles: Outsider (12), Guest of the shrine (50), Familiar face (120), Name in the paper (220), Solver of incidents (350), Legend of Gensokyo (500). What each title opens in the world is planned.
combat: Combat mode (R): with it on, the left button always attacks and the right button always guards. With it off, the buttons work as usual, but you still strike when you hold a weapon, when your hand is empty in a fight, or when an enemy is within a tool's swing. An empty hotbar slot means fists.

Chain of 5 blows: tap the left button for one blow, or hold it and the whole chain runs by itself. With the Bamboo Spear the chain is thrust, thrust, a five-hit flurry, a shaft spin that doubles the target over, and a final blow that throws it up: 9 hits in all. Inputs are buffered, so a press during a blow queues the next one.

Directional moves: W + attack is the Launcher (opens at Blade 5, together with two air blows); S + attack is a low blow that knocks down, or an execution on an enemy lying on the ground; holding toward a target + attack rushes in; tapping a side during the chain is the Branch, a sweep that leaves the target Exposed; S + attack in the air is a plunging dive.

A blow that would miss chases its target a short way, so distance alone does not save an enemy. Every blow makes the target reel; launched targets float before they fall, and downed ones lie on the ground for a while.
Run and sprint: walking (9 blocks a second) costs no Breath, in and out of fights. Double-tap A or D and hold to sprint at 13.5 blocks a second, spending 20 Breath a second.

Roll (Shift): a quick dodge of about 0.3 s that covers 5 blocks and costs 25 Breath; nothing hits you for most of it. Rolling through a blow just in time is a perfect dodge: the fight slows down for a moment and Guard gains experience.

Guard (hold right button in combat mode): blocks blows from the front and drains your Guard, which can be at most half of your current Breath. At zero your guard breaks: you reel, take double damage and cannot guard or roll until your Breath fills again. Blows from behind and bullets go through a guard.
Parry (Guard 5): raise a fresh guard up to 0.2 s before a blow lands. It cancels the damage, costs nothing, leaves the attacker open for a second, and your next blows hit harder.
Breath: every blow, roll and sprint costs Breath, which refills by itself shortly after you stop spending it. With too little Breath you cannot roll and your blows come out tired.
Lock (Ctrl): locks onto the nearest hostile in front of you, so your body and blows face it. Press Ctrl again to release; it also releases if the target dies or gets more than 16 blocks away.

Sheet of blows (G): a combo editor where you choose which moves fill each row (chain, up, down, toward, branch, air, dive, downed, holding, counter) for the weapon family in your hand. More slots open as Blade and Guard rise; you cannot edit it during a fight or with an enemy near.

Weapons: the Bamboo Spear, Bamboo Bow (hold to draw, release to shoot; uses Arrows) and Iron Blade, plus 192 more: 48 kinds, each in Copper, Iron, Gold and Diamond. The kinds include swords, katanas, scimitars, rapiers, daggers, cleavers, sickles, battle axes, double axes, spears, halberds, clubs, maces, flails, war hammers, scythes, eight elemental staffs (the gohei staff among them), eight grimoires, and firearms from pistols, revolvers and shotguns to SMGs, carbines, assault rifles, sniper rifles and energy guns. Copper weapons are made at the Carpenter's Table, the others at the Anvil as it is upgraded. Each family fights with its own set of moves, and tools hit with a single blow.

Enemies: the Boar youkai (medium weight; scrapes the ground, then charges straight through; drops Raw Meat and sometimes Boar Hide), the Crow youkai (light, flying; a shadow marks where it will dive; drops Feathers and sometimes Raw Meat) and the Fairy (light, flying; glows, then fires a fan of three slow bullets, and flees when hurt to half its Life; may drop Fairy Dust, Season Flowers and Seeds). Fairies and crows only appear by day; boars at any hour. These road enemies are not the peaceful fairies, crows and boars of the Bestiary.

Enemies never hurt you by touch: every attack is announced by a warning first, no more than two enemies attack at once, and none attacks from off screen. After you take damage you cannot be hit again for a moment.
Spoils fall on the ground as items and are picked up like anything else.

Permadeath: if your Life reaches 0 outside a duel, whether in a fight, from a fall, cold, drowning or lava, the save ends. Your body stays where it fell, and the save remains only as a memorial in the Continue list. A few paths in the Book of Races can turn a death into a rite instead.
Spell Card duels (one-on-one duels with combos and danmaku cards), energy techniques and the Spell Card meter are planned and not playable yet.
hud: Day plate (top left): a dial where the sun or moon crosses the sky with the torii in front, the day of the week and date, the time, a season icon and a sky icon, plus a button that opens the Calendar (C). A day lasts 24 real minutes at Normal speed.
Game speed tab (under the day plate): an hourglass with 1x, 2x and 4x; the active mode is lit. Click it or use + / -.
Queue button (next to the speed tab): opens the Action queue (L); a running sequence shows its progress below it.

Life and Breath (top right): a lacquered plate with the red Life bar over the green Breath bar, a camellia medallion that sheds petals as Life drops, and a paper tag with your Life number. Below a quarter of Life the bar pulses red and the medallion cracks.

In fights, a steel band over the Breath bar shows your Guard (it turns to cracked crimson when broken), a badge beside the medallion shows that combat mode is on, and a combo counter appears on the left while your hits land in a row.
Hotbar (bottom centre): 8 slots with icons and counts; the selected item's name appears above it when you switch. In combat mode it turns into the move strip of the weapon in hand.
Layer badge (right of the hotbar): FG Foreground (Q) or BG Background (Q). It hides where blocks cannot be edited, such as indoors.
Block cursor: marks the target cell and shows whether mining or placing is possible there.
Notices at the top of the screen explain refusals, such as "The shrine grounds are protected.", "Too far away." or "It needs something to rest on."
"Game saved" appears at the top right after each save.
Hints near doors and roads, for example "[E] Enter the shrine" or "Take the road (E)".
settings: Languages: English (default), Português (Brazilian Portuguese) and 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese). Change it any time from Settings; it never affects your saves.

Settings > General: Language, Master volume, Music, Effects, Fullscreen, Reduced flashes (removes flashing impact frames and colour drains in fights), Adult content (on/off), NPC chatter (None, Few, Normal, Many), and Licenses.
Settings > Touch: Touch controls (Auto, Always, Never), Button size, Opacity, Tap on world, Vibration, Push up to jump, Fill the screen.

Game speed (Normal 1x, Fast 2x, Super fast 4x) is chosen in game with + / - or the HUD tab and is kept in your save. It speeds up the whole world evenly, while text, menus and controls keep their real-time pace.
The pause menu (Esc) has Resume, Settings, Save and Exit, and a list of controls.
tips: The shrine is a safe haven: from the meadow at the foot of its stairway to the end of the courtyard, no enemies ever appear, and indoors is always safe.
Your first hour in Gensokyo is quiet: nothing hostile appears until an hour of game time after you arrive.
Nights are more dangerous: enemies are almost twice as likely to show up after dark. Fairies and crow youkai only come out by day, but boar youkai roam at any hour.

Watch for the warning: the boar scrapes the ground before charging (roll through it with Shift), the crow's shadow marks where it will dive (step aside), and a fairy glows before firing three slow bullets (walk between them).
Death is permanent. When the Life plate starts pulsing red, back off toward the shrine.
Food does not heal you yet: cooked dishes will restore Life once eating is added. Back away from a fight before your Life runs low.
Walking costs no Breath; only the double-tap sprint, rolls and blows spend it. Keep some Breath for a roll.
Felled trees drop twigs and wild grass gives Plant Fiber: craft torches by hand early, because daylight fades about a dozen blocks into a cave.
You do not need empty slots to mine: blocks and wood drop on the ground and are pulled in once you have room.
The game autosaves every 30 seconds, and Save and Exit saves on the spot.
